A brand-new poll just showed something that's never happened before.
Peter, look at this:
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_stp-20260927-2.Yuuu_8&amount=5&refcode=em20260927-1139&t=2&akid=1139%2E34582%2Ezja2Ed)
In his four campaigns for governor, Greg Abbott has never once been shown trailing in a statewide Texas poll. _That just changed._
**A brand-new poll just showed us ahead of Abbott by four points****,** while he's asking Texans for a fourth term. Not within range. Not closing the gap. Ahead. For the first time.
Here’s what’s happening: Texans are getting a clear look at what twelve years of Greg Abbott has actually cost them. Rising grocery bills. Rising property taxes. Data centers flooding the state while the people footing the bill get nothing back. And when they look at me, they’re seeing someone who’s spent her career fighting for Texas families — not just for the people at the top.
**None of this happens without you.** We are competitive in this race because of the 170,000 people who've chipped in to build this campaign. Our people-powered movement is working. We are clearly breaking through.
But Abbott has a firehose of money aimed at us — $67 million in the bank, and he's already outspent us 10-to-1. He's never had to run from behind before. With this poll out there, he's going to open that firehose all the way to drown out our campaign before Texans vote.
We can't match him dollar for dollar. But we can outnumber him — that's how we got here. 170,000 donors have helped build this campaign into one that can win.
I’m asking every one of you to dig a little deeper, right now, to keep us competitive.

Capital Rotation — September 27, 2026
Nothing New to Price Over the Weekend. Monday Decides Whether the Yield Story Keeps Its Streak.
Markets sat out a weekend of harder rhetoric between Washington and Tehran with nothing new to actually price. The real test comes Monday: does the 10-year yield's four-session climb extend into a fifth, and how much of the coming week is month-end noise versus signal?
|
---
| | What Moved
---|---
**Verified fact:** markets were closed over the weekend following Friday's close — Dow +0.93% to 51,828.62, S&P; 500 +0.51% to 7,743.41, Nasdaq +0.48% to 27,068.72 — with the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.18%, its highest since the 2008 financial crisis, on a fourth consecutive session of climbing. Over the weekend, Iran's leadership hardened its public rejection of Trump's rejection, with no scheduled economic data or market-moving events before Monday's reopen.
| | Rotation Signal 01 — A Weekend of Harder Rhetoric, No New Market-Moving Facts
---|---
**Our interpretation:** Trump's “losing so badly” comment and Pezeshkian's “no longer trusted” statement are meaningful for the diplomatic narrative this newsletter has tracked all week, but neither constitutes new information markets can price beyond what was already known Friday — the proposal is rejected, Iran hasn't walked away, and no counter-offer exists. Monday's reopen is more likely to move on the yield curve's own momentum than on the weekend's rhetoric.
| | Rotation Signal 02 — The Yield Curve Enters Its Fifth Potential Session as the Dominant Story
---|---
**Verified fact:** the 10-year's climb to 5.18% marked four consecutive sessions of multi-decade highs through Friday, occurring independent of both positive and negative headlines across the week. **Our interpretation:** absent a genuine new catalyst over the weekend, the base case for Monday is a continuation of that structural pattern rather than a reversal driven by the Iran rhetoric — investors positioned for further yield strength have, if anything, had that thesis reinforced rather than challenged by the weekend's news.
| | Rotation Signal 03 — Positioning Into Month-End Adds a Second, Independent Variable
---|---
**Current classification: PRESSURE unresolved and rhetorically sharper on Iran; CONFIRMATION of structural yield repricing entering a fifth session.** With September's final trading days approaching, month-end and quarter-end rebalancing flows are likely to interact with both the Iran standoff and the rates story in ways that may be difficult to disentangle from the underlying fundamentals in the coming week's price action.
| | What to Watch This Week
---|---
Whether the 10-year yield extends its climb into a fifth consecutive session at Monday's open; whether Iran's mediator-channel response, once public, contains any actual movement on the sequencing dispute rather than a restatement of hardened rhetoric; and how much of the coming week's moves are attributable to month-end flows versus the underlying Iran and rates narratives.

clean_body: We’ve got to double down on our work for fair representation ahead of Election Day | = Peter, Stateline is reporting that Democrats have a real chance this year to flip control of several state legislatures — often our last lines of defense against Republican gerrymandering. The truth is, most of the country isn’t paying attention to these state-level fights. But if you’re reading this, you know how important these races are. The NDRC has identified eight priority states — Arizona, Georgia, Minnesota, New Hampshire, Pennsylvania, Texas, Washington, and Wisconsin — where Democrats have a good chance to build long-term power in the state legislature and even flip some chambers from Republican control. Republican-controlled state legislatures passed unprecedented mid-decade map redraws at the direction of Donald Trump. Other GOP legislatures rushed to pass new gerrymanders after the Supreme Court gutted key voting rights protections. And leaders in many other states are already planning to ramp up this cynical redraw strategy ahead of 2028. That’s why we’re investing in over 250 of the most critical state-level races. body:
We’ve come too far to slow down now

The midterm elections are in 6 short weeks. The polls are _too_ close.
The clock is ticking.

The Deep Regime File — September 27, 2026
Harder Words, Same Process: What the Iran Rhetoric Escalation Actually Changed
Trump and Iran's leadership traded their sharpest language of the week over the rejected Hormuz plan. Neither side broke the underlying mediated process. Markets reopen Monday with a clean, low-noise test of whether the yield curve's four-session climb is structural or just waiting for a headline that finally moves it.
|
---
| | The Setup
---|---
This newsletter closed Saturday's edition asking whether Tehran would respond to Trump's rejection with escalation or a revised offer. The weekend answered with a third option this newsletter had not explicitly weighted: sharper public rhetoric from both governments, paired with no change to the underlying mediated process and no new economic action from either side.
| | Development One — Both Leaders Escalated Language Without Escalating Substance
---|---
**Verified fact:** Trump said Iran's plan “would not be acceptable” and that Iran wants a deal only “because they are losing so badly.” Araghchi said Iran “will not back down” and called Trump's statements historically “contradictory”; Pezeshkian said Tehran “no longer trusted” negotiations with Washington. **Verified fact:** despite this, Iran is still routing its formal response through mediators rather than declaring the process over, and Washington has not offered a counter-proposal or announced new military action. **Our interpretation:** the gap between hardened public rhetoric and an unchanged private process is itself informative — it suggests both governments are managing domestic political pressure (a midterms-conscious White House, an Iranian public asked to accept continued hardship) without yet being willing to abandon the mediated channel entirely. **What remains unknown** is how long that gap can persist before rhetoric either de-escalates back toward the negotiating table or hardens into an actual breakdown of the mediator channel.
| | Development Two — Washington's Lack of a Counter-Offer May Be the More Consequential Choice
---|---
**Verified fact:** as of this writing, no alternative U.S. proposal has surfaced, and Trump's public comments suggest comfort with the status quo rather than urgency to negotiate. **Our interpretation:** pairing a rejection with no counter-offer, on top of Friday's reported aide comments about a midterms-timed bombing campaign, reads as Washington judging that continued military and sanctions pressure serves its position better than a fresh proposal right now — a strategic choice, if accurate, that shifts the burden of the next concrete move onto Tehran rather than Washington.
| | Development Three — Markets Enter the Week With the Yield Story Unbroken and Untested
---|---
**Verified fact:** Friday's close left the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.18%, a fourth consecutive session of multi-decade highs, with no weekend catalyst to interrupt that trend before Monday's reopen. **Our interpretation:** if this newsletter's read of the yield move as structural rather than headline-driven is correct, a weekend of purely rhetorical escalation — with no new economic or military facts — should be exactly the kind of news that fails to move it, making Monday's open a genuine, low-noise test of that thesis.
| | Why This Sits at the Center of the Board
---|---
**Current classification: PRESSURE unresolved on Iran, now rhetorically sharper on both sides but procedurally unchanged; CONFIRMATION of structural yield repricing awaiting its fifth-session test.** The throughline this newsletter has tracked since Thursday is a widening gap between what governments and markets say and what they actually do — harder words on Iran without a broken process, and yields that keep climbing regardless of whether the week's other headlines are read as good news or bad.
| | What Would Change the Classification
---|---
On Iran: any sign the mediator channel itself is breaking down, rather than public rhetoric hardening around an unchanged process, or any concrete U.S. counter-proposal. On rates: whether Monday's open extends the yield climb to a fifth session on no new catalyst, which would be the cleanest confirmation yet that this is a structural move rather than a headline-driven one. On markets broadly: how cleanly month-end and quarter-end flows can be separated from the underlying Iran and rates narratives as September closes out.

On rates: whether Monday's open extends the yield climb to a fifth session on no new catalyst, which would be the cleanest confirmation yet that this is a structural move rather than a headline-driven one. On markets broadly: how cleanly month-end and quarter-end flows can be separated from the underlying Iran and rates narratives as September closes out. | | | (ad by Behind the Markets) | | | At Deep Regime Trends, we write for people who think for themselves. name: Roy Cooper
subject: Laying all our cards on the table
body:
With Senate control at stake, every single dollar really, truly counts.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1441&source=&t=1&akid=3883%2E124072%2E4IcPrg) | | | |
---
Peter – I have nowhere else to turn right now.
This Wednesday at midnight is our last quarterly FEC reporting deadline before the election, after which we’re required by law to share our fundraising totals publicly. We have three days left to raise the last $1.8 million we need, and we’re running out of time.
Experts at Politico say Democratic Senate control hinges on winning in North Carolina, and the NYT reports our campaign is the best chance we have to flip a red seat blue.
**However, that could all change if we fall short Wednesday night.** The GOP is trying to buy my Trump-backed opponent’s way to victory, and now, two recent polls show Michael Whatley in striking distance of taking the lead.
Republicans are pouring tens of millions into false attack ads – amplifying the President’s lies about me – and if we’re not able to fight back, they will overwhelm our grassroots movement.
So in a race this critical, every single dollar really, truly counts. Too much is on the line.
[**_Can I please count on you to chip in $5, $10 – whatever you can tonight – to help me hit my end-of-quarter goal and win the U.S. Senate race in North Carolina?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1441&amount=5&t=8&akid=3883%2E124072%2E4IcPrg)
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [DONATE $5](https://act.roycooper.com/go/16105?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1441&amount=5&t=9&akid=3883%2E124072%2E4IcPrg)
---
| | [DONATE $25](https://act.roycooper.com/go/16105?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1441&amount=25&t=10&akid=3883%2E124072%2E4IcPrg)
---
| | [DONATE $50](https://act.roycooper.com/go/16105?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1441&amount=50&t=11&akid=3883%2E124072%2E4IcPrg)
---
| | [OTHER AMOUNT](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1441&t=12&akid=3883%2E124072%2E4IcPrg)
---
We have a real chance to win this race and show the GOP that North Carolina’s seat is not for sale. Your continued support is a huge part of that.
Thanks so much for being on this team.
Roy Cooper
| |
* * *
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1441&t=2&akid=3883%2E124072%2E4IcPrg)
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

[**_Donate today to help win this seat and flip the Senate blue._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1441&source=&t=3&akid=3883%2E124072%2E4IcPrg)

# [Pro-lifers Don’t Really Care About “Life of the Mother”](https://bethfarnhamforcongress.com/2026/09/27/pro-lifers-dont-really-care-about-life-of-the-mother/?jetpack_skip_subscription_popup)
---
By **Elizabeth Farnham** on September 27, 2026
---
| **District Round-up 09.27.26**
---
Dear Neighbor, Thank you for reading my District Round-up. As your candidate for Pennsylvania’s 13th Congressional District, it is my honor and pleasure to deliver to you where I’ve been and what issues I’ve tackled in the past week. Criss-crossing the counties of Adams, Franklin, Fulton, Bedford, Cambria, Blair, Huntingdon, Mifflin, Juniata, Perry, Cumberland, and Somerset gives me great opportunities to meet with voters, hear what is on your hearts and minds, and the chance to voice my fight for Everyday Americans. If you would like to contribute to my campaign, please donate here:**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/beth-farnham-for-congress-1](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=f5f3c55e6e1842bec2e89a5025bd1c97d0d7d229a6c39a93c9d7d38f44782551&blog_id=213069660&post_id=9090&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=0c58cef2420522916ed439b4f85b1c9c&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL2JldGgtZmFybmhhbS1mb3ItY29uZ3Jlc3MtMQ=&email_id=d9fbb41ae2e312d3b8a96de2d07dbfdb)**
---
| **Hidden Maternal Mortality Rate**
---
| |
---
“Life of the mother” is the cry of pro-lifers as their touted exception to abortion bans, but they don’t really mean it.
---
Ever since Roe v. Wade was overturned in 2022, many conservative states imposed very restrictive abortion bans, based on the heartbeat bill that Texas created in 2021, using vague language surrounding the process to override the ban in the event that a mother’s life was at risk.
---
Since doctors wouldn’t risk their licensure and loss of freedom to 99 years in prison on the chance that legislators wouldn’t approve the abortion, they delayed care to those in need. Maternal mortality rates leapt in Texas so much so, they decided to delay the reports.
---
And the mothers continued to die.
---
Josseli Barnica was one such mother. Like 60% of those who seek abortion, she was actually already a mother, and this was a wanted pregnancy. But the fetus had miscarried, opening her cervix, exposing her uterus to dangerous bacteria. However, it still had a heartbeat and because of that, doctors would not perform the necessary operation to save her life. No one could save the fetus, and three days later, no one could save her from the sepsis that followed.
---
Because a fetus had a heartbeat, a woman who wanted more children died and her daughter was left without a mother.
---
Now we learn that Texas will not release the reports on maternal mortality for 2022-2023 until after the midterms.
---
Why?
---

Corporations won’t be able to force their employees to watch “Right to Work” nonsense and no corporation will be able to deny union membership. I’ll also advocate a national healthcare plan so workers won’t have to settle for jobs they hate to have their basic healthcare needs met. President Biden once said, “The middle class built America and the unions built the middle class,” and he wasn’t wrong. The good jobs have the wages and benefits they do because of the sacrifices of many union workers across the generations. Working Families deserve the rights, wages, and working conditions that ensure work-life balance and dignity in retirement. I can’t wait to represent them in Congress. Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and American workers! (Photo credit:Tim Buck) | | ---|--- | | Town Hall in Gettysburg | | ---|--- Many thanks to The People’s Town Hall of Gettysburg for hosting the Town Hall today at The Barn Resort. I appreciate the opportunity to have answered questions about Big Tech, town halls, and public education from District 13 residents. Fellow candidates and Todd Crawley did a fantastic job answering questions. Of course, none of the Republican incumbents were brave enough to participate, and our own US Representative, multimillionaire John Joyce, couldn’t be bothered to even observe courtesy to decline. No worries. He’s fired anyway. Elect me, Beth Farnham, to represent our beautiful 13th Congressional District because you know that not only will I vote in the interests of Everyday Americans, I’ll show up for you too. Together, we and real representation! Photo credits: Sue Obe and Jack Stansbury Thank you to for having streamed it live and posting the recording that is shared below. | Heritage Festival | | Sunday was a lovely day to celebrate Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion in Adams County. Many thanks to the Adams County Heritage Festival Committee for hosting another successful year of festive music, delicious food, and rich culture. I spoke at length with our new Democratic Commissioner, Mark Clowney, caught up with dear friends, and encouraged new voters to vote for me. Together, we and Community! (Photo credit: Jack Stansbury) | | | ---|---|--- | Grateful for Local Support | | Many thanks to all who turned out for Thursday night’s fundraiser! Thank you to the fundraiser committee of Lois, Cookie, Edie, Nancy, and Meghan who made this possible and worked throughout! Thank you to Team Beth Farnham for Congress members and volunteers Jack, Sandy, Sue, and Joyce who greeted guests and helped guests have yard signs, postcards, and other ways to promote the campaign! Thank you to Ben Kennedy for playing piano! Thank you to Chef Amy for delicious nibbles! It was a lovely evening of support and connection. And if you would like to donate to the campaign, follow the link below! Together, we #ChooseDemocracy and real representation! Photo credit: Sandy Hartzell and Sue Obie | | ---|--- | AMAZING REPRESENTATION! | | What an AMAZING day! Many thanks to Team Beth Farnham volunteers who made our presence known in 3 counties all at once on Saturday. In Mercersburg, campaign manager Jack Stansbury and other volunteers fought the wind to deliver literature and yard signs to voters. In Thompsontown, Sandy Hartzell and volunteers, including Juniata County Democratic Committee Chair Spencer McLaughlin worked to acquaint voters with the campaign. In Ebensburg, I worked with several volunteers to help voters at the Potatofest know what’s at stake – the soul of our nation, for example. It was a great time to hand out yard signs, literature, and bumper stickers. Together, we Democracy and visibility! Photo credits: Jack Stansbury and Sandy Hartzell | | | Jack worked hard to organize it ahead of time. ---|---|--- | | | ---|---|--- | Charity of the Week! Even though charitable donations will not meet the overwhelming need of food assistance and healthcare for lower income Americans, these charities are a stopgap until I am elected to the U.S. House of Representatives and can legislate helpful federal programs as well as prevent a rapacious president from illegally impounding the congressionally-approved funds for those programs. Please check out the Manos Unidas Hispanic-American Center, Inc. page and donate to them, if you can. website – donation link – | | | Comparing and Contrasting Votes on Legislation Check out how Joyce recently voted, how I would have voted in comparison, and why! FYI – if you’re having trouble seeing this comparison in your email, please click the option for “Read on Blog” and it will load properly for you. | | If you’re like me, you love this country as much as I do and work to make a positive difference. In the midst of this Constitutional Crisis, please consider reaching out to your county Democratic committee or Democratic candidates so that we can strengthen our Democracy instead of letting it slide into fascism. We don’t just #ChooseDemocracy, we choose Pennsylvania, we choose The United States of America, we choose Humanity and I am deeply glad to work along side you. We’re in the final sprint, folks.
That means I am either on the road talking about our plan to make Wisconsin a better place to live, work, and raise a family, or fundraising (and spending whatever time is left with my family).
This race will be a close race, Derek. Wisconsin always comes down to just a few votes. So every dollar we can put on the air or online matters a ton.
**Here is the thing: We're currently TIED in the polls, and billionaire families are bankrolling Tom Tiffany's campaign.**
**My team is worried we won't meet our goals. That's why I'm emailing you so late. I need you to chip in right now.**
**[Please, next week's deadline matters more than most. All of our fundraising numbers will become public. The **good news** is that national election forecasters upgraded our chances of winning, and a new poll shows us up by _2 points!_

name: Karl VonZabern
subject: We Need to Get AI Right - Eric Jones for Congress
body:
Hi everyone,
With so much attention recently in the news on AI safety, we believe it is important that we at the Eric Jones campaign are clear about our position on AI.

AI is here and is already causing disruptions to our economy and society. We believe strongly that we need to regulate AI based on five core principles.
**1\. Protect workers.** AI will take real jobs in this district. A generation ago, Washington let globalization ship our work overseas and abandoned the families left behind. Eric won't let automation repeat that mistake. He will require that workers get advance notice and a real say before machines replace them, and he will tax the corporations profiting most from automation to fund union-powered training and new career paths.
**2\. Stop data centers from raising your bills** Data centers consume enormous amounts of electricity and water, and you pay for it through higher utility bills. Eric will fight for a moratorium on new data centers in California. Everywhere else, new data centers must generate their own clean power on site and meet strict water standards.
**3\. Make Big Tech pay its fair share.** Amazon paid zero federal income tax in 2018. Eric will close the loopholes so tech giants pay their share, just like nurses, teachers, and small businesses do.
**4\. Give you ownership of your data**. Big Tech tracks where you go, what you say, and what you buy, then sells it. Eric will fight for a federal privacy law and an AI Bill of Rights so no one can take, sell, or use your information without your consent.
**5\. Keep a few companies from owning AI and our government.** Concentrated wealth buys political power. Eric will enforce antitrust law, protect open competition, and get corporate money out of politics. We can't hold Big Tech accountable while it can buy the referees. We can have another government sanctioned for profit monopoly in AI.
We are witnessing an incredible advancement in technology that has many benefits, however we need to make sure that the gains from AI reach everyone, not just a few.
If these priorities matter to you, help us spread the word. Join us for a phone bank or door knock this month.
**Sign up here:**
**Phone bank:** ericjones.us/volunteer/phonecalls
**Door Knocking:** ericjones.us/volunteer/doorknocking
All the best,

**Karl VonZabern, PhD**
**
**
**Regional Field Director**
**Eric Jones For Congress**
**karl@ericjones.us**

subject: I have a message for Peter.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
Why Texas? I’ll tell you why.
#
Hi Peter, it’s Maria Teresa.
Every election cycle, people ask me the same question: _Why focus on Texas?_
[**I’ll tell you why, but first, will you donate any amount right now to support Voto Latino’s work?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/305?c0=em-ms-voto-20260928-1.Nyr4Qm&refcode=em20260928-626&t=1&akid=626%2E1366028%2EwanL3i)
I was recently on MS NOW sharing why Texas is so critical to the future of our country, and why empowering the Latino electorate in the Lone Star State is our _highest_ priority.
And my answer for why I think we should focus on Texas is simple, Peter. As the Latino vote goes, so goes the White House, Congress, and the Senate.
[](https://act.votolatino.org/go/305?c0=em-ms-voto-20260928-1.Nyr4Qm&refcode=em20260928-626&t=2&akid=626%2E1366028%2EwanL3i)
Texas is home to one of the largest, most dynamic Latino electorates in the nation, and makes up 40% of the state population. **To put it plainly, Latinos are a driving force in shaping America's future.**
Also, Texas added more than 950,000 voters between recent election cycles alone, making it a cornerstone of American democracy.
Transforming demographic growth into lasting civic power requires intentional, on-the-ground engagement. **Nationwide, 1 in 3 young voters is unregistered. And in Texas, that gap is even wider, leaving 3 in 5 young adults off the voter rolls.**
Young people care deeply about student debt, climate change, good jobs, and healthcare. Turning those priorities into policy takes fundamental first steps, like registering to vote and building a plan to cast a ballot. But that work requires resources and a ton of work — especially in these final 6 days before Texas’s October 5th voter registration deadline.
**[Peter, will you make a donation of $5, $10, $25, or any amount you can today to help us register young voters in Texas before October 5th?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/305?c0=em-ms-voto-20260928-1.Nyr4Qm&refcode=em20260928-626&t=3&akid=626%2E1366028%2EwanL3i)**
**[Donate $3 ››](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260928-1.6AxDnu&amount=3&refcode=20260928-626&t=22&akid=626%2E1366028%2EwanL3i)**
Thank you,
Maria Teresa Kumar

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ms-voto-footer?refcode=em20260928-626-&t=23&refcode2=626_1366028_wanL3i&akid=626%2E1366028%2EwanL3i)**
---
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way we keep in touch with people like you, so thank you for reading to the end.

On November 3rd, we must elect a Congress that will end this heartless chaos
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2463%2E791427%2EnL_9xT)
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-sep26.biBhTt&refcode=em260928-1-subs&t=2&akid=2463%2E791427%2EnL_9xT)
---
**Friend, it’s Congresswoman Ilhan Omar. I’m humbly, respectfully asking for just a minute of your time.**
I’ve been under attack from Trump and all of MAGA since he took office last year.
He’s launched constant racist attacks at me and Somali-Americans. He’s opened sham investigations into me and threatened my deportation. He called me “garbage.”
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-sep26.biBhTt&refcode=em260928-1-subs&t=3&akid=2463%2E791427%2EnL_9xT)
But these personal attacks are nothing compared to what Trump did next.
ICE surged into Minnesota — a brazen retaliation by the federal government against a state that has defied Trump’s authoritarianism. **My heart still aches from what I saw.**
My neighbors profiled and harassed. My constituents beaten and abused. Citizens and immigrants alike stolen of their civil rights. Parents afraid to even take their kids to school. Thousands of regular people caught up in a needless and inhumane immigration operation.
And then, the unthinkable happened: _Two of my constituents were murdered by ICE agents while exercising their right to protest._
The reality is, ICE’s violence hasn’t stopped. Even though they may have drawn down in Minnesota and the media has moved on, countless lives are still changed for the worse by ICE each and every day. More people have died under Trump’s watch and many more are stuck in cruel conditions in detention camps.
**On November 3rd, we must elect a Congress that will end this heartless chaos and bring consequences down on everyone involved, including the President.**
**I’m doing everything I can to support progressive candidates up and down the ballot, especially here in Minnesota where we have critical statewide races to win. I’m asking for your help before our final quarterly FEC deadline of the midterms.**
[**Will you join me in this fight by making a donation to my campaign today? We have to make sure that what’s happened to Minnesota — and what’s happening across the country — never happens again. MassGOP Statement on Montano's in Truro Situation
Statement from Amy Carnevale, Chairwoman Massachusetts Republican Party
A Cape Cod restaurant served as a venue for a lawful gathering for two candidates running for political office.
For that, Montano's in Truro received hate mail, threats that the building should burn down, and a hoax 911 call that sent emergency vehicles and a State Police helicopter to a fake emergency designed to interfere with restaurant operations.
The owner has said Montano's rents its space to many groups and does not discriminate based on political views. Providing a venue for an event designed to foster free association is not an endorsement. It is a private business doing what a free country allows.
Now reverse the parties. If Democrats had hosted that event and then faced the same threats and a fake 911 call, the same voices would demand a full investigation. They would be right. The standard should not change because the candidates were Republicans.
This is about whether the public square still exists. Attacking a private business for providing a venue for a political event you dislike is not defending democracy. It is intolerance. Speech is not free if it is only safe when one side agrees with it.
The Massachusetts Republican Party calls for a full investigation of the threats and the hoax call. Charge the people who did this. And every elected official who lectures the country about democracy should say, without hedging, that a small business may host any lawful political event without being punished for it. If that principle only applies when Democrats are in the room, it is not a principle. It is a racket.

name: Wes Moore
subject: I know what it’s like to need someone to believe in you.
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2004%2E1086043%2EunL-h4)
Peter, let me tell you why I have dedicated my life to public service.
This is a longer message, so if you don’t have time to read through, I would appreciate **[a donation to power our campaign before our end-of-quarter deadline.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260928-1.p7pz8F&refcode=em-20260928-1&t=2&akid=2004%2E1086043%2EunL-h4)**
**I know what it’s like to need someone to believe in you.**
I lost my father at a young age, had handcuffs on my wrist by age 11, and watched my mom work tirelessly to support our family. I grew up facing challenges that could have defined the rest of my life.
But those challenges didn’t define me.
There were people who saw me for more than my circumstances. They believed in me, opened doors for me, and reminded me that my future wasn’t already written.
**I’ll never forget where I came from, and I never stop thinking about the kids growing up today who just need someone to believe in them too.**
That’s why we’ve worked to build a Maryland that leaves no one behind: making historic investments in our public schools, expanding opportunities for everyone, and making sure all Marylanders have the chance to succeed.
There’s still so much more to do, and the work that lies ahead will take all of us. With our end-of-quarter deadline just days away, I need you by my side to be able to continue this mission.
**[If you’re able, will you chip in $5, $25, or whatever you can before the September 30 deadline to help us keep making Maryland a place where everyone has a fair shot?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260928-1.p7pz8F&refcode=em-20260928-1&t=3&akid=2004%2E1086043%2EunL-h4)**

Elevate,
Wes

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Vivek Ramaswamy and Rob McColley for Ohio
body:
I will never take your sacrifice for granted.

| [](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
---
Politics today is full of noise – phony deadlines, scare tactics, and cheap gimmicks.
But I want to cut through the noise for a moment.
[I’d like to tell you a quick story.](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.-58A)
I grew up right here in Ohio. My parents worked hard to give me a chance at the American Dream, and I know what sacrifice looks like. Every opportunity I’ve had was built on the back of that sacrifice.
---
[](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)
---
That’s why I never forget what it means when someone like you chips in a few dollars. It isn’t “just money.” **
**It’s trust. It’s belief. It’s a vote of confidence in the movement we’re building in Ohio and beyond. **
**So whether you’ve already donated or you’re considering it today, let me say this clearly: **
**[THANK YOU, Peter!](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.)**
**We’re in an extremely tough fight. And this isn’t just any race – it’s shaping up to be the most important in the country.**
**I threw my hat in the ring now because we have a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to save our country. I mean that. We were[ ONE ELECTION AWAY](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.) from a country you and I wouldn’t recognize anymore.**
**President Trump saved us – with the help of folks like you – from that dire outcome. With that said, he needs loyal partners at the state level to help him succeed. **
**That’s why this race means so much. **
**So if you’ve given before (even just once, even just a buck) know this: you’ve already made a difference, and I will never take your sacrifice for granted. **
**And if you haven’t given yet –[ and you’re able to spare even $1 today](https://trk.email.vivekforohio.) – I’d be honored to have you on my team.
Every single gift, no matter the size, fuels this must-win fight.

Dear Patriot,
**Victorville, California. 4:45 in the morning.** A man walks out of his house in the dark and drives toward a gas station a few minutes down the road. Federal agents are already behind him. **No chase. No standoff. What impact will AI have on inequality?
A couple months ago, I was asked to debate 20 AI optimists for a broadly watched online series "Surrounded." You've probably seen the thumbnails on YouTube or other platforms; a person sits on a chair literally surrounded by people who want to take the opposite point of view. These things get a LOT of views, and I've always wanted to debate 20 people at once. So, I said yes.
I agreed to back the following 4 statements:
1\. AI will not democratize opportunity; it will accelerate inequality on a scale we have never seen before.
2\. AI is going to eliminate millions of jobs faster than new ones can be created.
3\. Universal Basic Income will become necessary as AI reduces the need for human labor.
4\. The market will optimize for productivity and profit, not human dignity.
And so, weeks later, I turned up to a repurposed warehouse in Los Angeles and dutifully sat in the middle of a circle of adults, who would rush to the center to debate me on whichever statement above they felt most strongly negatively about. The other participants actually were not told ahead of time who they were debating, but some of them guessed it was going to be me based on the topic. You can see the result [here](https://substack.com/redirect/0e2fb2d5-e8e0-4303-aff6-6ed03c6d052f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/64034858-322d-4ecc-bd37-477abe01c3e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I have been hitting a similar message on various TV networks for weeks (or years, depending on how you look at it), as AI has dominated headlines. It came out this week that rogue bots from OpenAI may have altered government websites here in the U.S., the latest in a string of disturbing new reports. The latest discussion has been around "Will AI kill us all?" which is definitely a compelling topic. But looming is the impact of automating away millions of white-collar knowledge sector jobs on both individuals and communities. Entry-level coding and customer service jobs have already started to disappear, and colleges this week announced price cuts in an attempt to keep students coming.
25% of small, private colleges are going to close or merge in the next ten years, which is going to be disastrous for the towns they're based in. The compression of the knowledge premium associated with having a college degree is going to be savage and unkind for many, particularly the young.
The above is going to drive anti-AI sentiment to new heights; Bernie Sanders has already proposed a ban on superintelligence. One danger is that this current automation wave becomes politicized; college graduates tend to skew Democratic, and being anti-college has overlapped with Trumpism over the past 10 years.
This is, of course, idiotic. Technology doesn't care about the partisan leanings of a set of workers; it just wants to eliminate inefficiencies. Unfortunately, a lot more of us will find ourselves in that boat.
You can put me in the camp of intelligent guardrails, but I've always felt an urgency to share the abundance created by AI as quickly as possible. Employees within Anthropic are going to become rich beyond imagining in approximately 6 weeks when their IPO hits. Meanwhile, the vast majority of Americans are going to feel like the future is being built without them. They're not wrong. Changing that has to be the main priority.
I interview Tom Krumins, the co-founder and CEO of CampaignAI, this week on the [podcast](https://substack.com/redirect/56612c6c-aad1-4b8a-aa5e-f4bb5472145d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). **Part I: The founding-era**
For the first century of the republic there was no federal immigration law at all. The Naturalization Act of 1790 restricted citizenship to "free white persons" -- it said nothing about who could arrive. The first real immigration statutes (Page Act 1875, Chinese Exclusion Act 1882) targeted Chinese laborers, not the Middle East. Nobody in 1789, 1820, or 1860 was turned away for being Syrian, Persian, or Ottoman, because there was no rule to turn them away under.
What did govern Middle Easterners was the "free white person" clause -- and the courts consistently put Arabs on the white side of the line. In 'In re Najour' (1909), 'In re Mudarri' (1910), and 'Dow v. United States' (1915), federal courts ruled that Syrians and Lebanese were white and therefore eligible to naturalize. A Syrian-born Muslim, 'Ex parte Mohriez' (1944), was naturalized on the same logic. That's why a real Middle Eastern community existed in America long before 1924: tens of thousands of Syrians and Lebanese (Ottoman subjects -- mostly Christians, but also Muslims and Druze) arrived between the 1880s and 1920, built peddler networks, opened businesses, founded the first mosques -- Ross, North Dakota (1929) and Cedar Rapids, Iowa (1934) -- and became citizens.
So the founding-era never disallowed it. The first Middle Eastern immigrants were naturalizing as U.S. citizens before the Titanic sailed.

Peter, My grandfather came home from the Second World War and walked into the General Motors plant in Warren. He stayed thirty-three years.
My father pinned on a badge in Oakland County. He is still wearing it, thirty-eight years later.
I went to Michigan State, took a commission out of ROTC, and spent nearly ten years in the Army — the 82nd Airborne, the 101st, nine months in Baghdad, and a Bronze Star I still don't really know how to talk about.
_**Three generations. One family.**_ Every bit of it inside the lines of this district.

My family taught me that service isn't a slogan. It's a duty. Nobody in my house was ever handed anything — my grandfather built cars, my dad answered calls at three in the morning, and I went where the Army sent me. I'm asking you to help me keep that going.
Here's where things stand. The Democrats have targeted this seat because they believe it's how they win the House back. My opponent burned through nearly every dollar she raised just getting through her primary, so the national party is about to step in and fund her.
And here I am, asking regular people for **a dollar.**
**Honestly? That's how I'd rather do it.** _**September 30th is the last end-of-quarter deadline of this campaign.**_ What we raise pays for yard signs across Macomb, gas in the tank for our door-knockers, and coffee for the volunteers who show up on Saturday mornings for nothing.
I'm not going to ask you to dig deep.
_**[$3. That's it. clean_body: My grandfather's plant is inside these lines| | | Peter, My grandfather came home from the Second World War and walked into the General Motors plant in Warren. He stayed thirty-three years. My father pinned on a badge in Oakland County. He is still wearing it, thirty-eight years later. I went to Michigan State, took a commission out of ROTC, and spent nearly ten years in the Army — the 82nd Airborne, the 101st, nine months in Baghdad, and a Bronze Star I still don't really know how to talk about. Three generations. One family. Every bit of it inside the lines of this district. My family taught me that service isn't a slogan. It's a duty. Nobody in my house was ever handed anything — my grandfather built cars, my dad answered calls at three in the morning, and I went where the Army sent me. I'm asking you to help me keep that going. Here's where things stand. The Democrats have targeted this seat because they believe it's how they win the House back. My opponent burned through nearly every dollar she raised just getting through her primary, so the national party is about to step in and fund her. And here I am, asking regular people for a dollar. Honestly? That's how I'd rather do it. September 30th is the last end-of-quarter deadline of this campaign. What we raise pays for yard signs across Macomb, gas in the tank for our door-knockers, and coffee for the volunteers who show up on Saturday mornings for nothing. I'm not going to ask you to dig deep. My family taught me that service isn't a slogan, it's a duty. I would be grateful for ANYTHING you can send. Please donate below! ⬇️ Whatever you can do. [1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

In case you missed it: Justice Democrat Justin J. Pearson was recently
featured on Mother Jones’ podcast More to the Story.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260928-1-jjp.fsommV&refcode=em20260928-38300&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1002&akid=38300%2E1203867%2ErbCVVn ]Image of Justin J. Pearson holding and speaking into a megaphone.
Caption: "The fight for America's future is happening in the South"

As Justin told host Al Letson, “The litmus test for America’s future is
what happens in the South. And so we need to be paying attention to what’s
going on here, because here is where the test cases for autocracy happen.
Here is where the billionaires have their testing ground for what else can
go on in other parts of the country.”

And he’s right,
Peter.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260928-1-jjp.fsommV&refcode=em20260928-38300&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1003&akid=38300%2E1203867%2ErbCVVn ]If you stand with Justin, will you rush a split contribution of
$10 to his campaign and Justice Democrats before Wednesday’s
final end-of-quarter deadline?

Justin is at the center of some of the biggest national political fights
happening right now, from data centers to racist gerrymandering.

When the Tennessee GOP redrew the state’s only majority-black district out
of existence this year, they expected Justin to pack up and walk away from
his race for Congress. He refused to surrender our democracy to
billionaire-backed Jim Crow tactics.

Instead, he got out there, united working people across different
backgrounds, and won the Democratic primary. Now, Justin is working to
out-organize his far-right Trump-backed opponent in November’s general
election and stop Republicans from diluting the political power of his
community.

Meanwhile, Justin has been leading the fight against tech billionaire Elon
Musk’s massive, polluting data centers that compromise the health of
majority-Black neighborhoods in South Memphis — an area that has
historically faced environmental racism and exploitation.

And he continues to speak out against the unconstitutional deployment of
the National Guard and ICE agents’ terrorizing operations in Memphis.

Make no mistake: blue cities and states across the country aren’t safe
from the authoritarianism being tested in red states like Tennessee.
What’s happening in Memphis can happen anywhere, and it’s up to us to
stand with fighters like Justin to stop it from spreading.

This November, we can send Justin to Congress to strengthen his fight
against Big Tech, MAGA white supremacy, and the corporate-backed
establishment keeping working families down — but only with grassroots
support from people like you,
Peter.

to help him win and finally give TN-09 the bold leader it deserves.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

clean_body: Peter, My name is Emily, and I'm a ballot chaser for Turning Point PAC in Arizona. That means every day, I show up, knock on doors, have conversations with potential voters, and chase down ballots before Election Day. I need to tell you what I'm seeing out here, because I don't think most people understand how close this really is. Arizona is not lost.Not even close. But it is not safe either. A new poll just showed Katie Hobbs up by 4 points over Andy Biggs. Four points. That is the entire ballgame, sitting right there behind the doors I have not knocked on yet. Turning Point PAC is not like anything else in this space. They take decades of grassroots organizing and put real people, like me, into these communities well before Election Day. We build relationships. We knock on the same doors more than once. We chase every ballot, mail-in or in person, because every single one counts. This is the vision Charlie Kirk built. People on the ground, having real conversations, changing real minds. And it is working! But I cannot do this alone, and neither can the 700 of us out here across Arizona. I 'm seeing momentum on the ground, but we have so many more voters to cover. We can't do it without your continued support. Every $50 you give sponsors a ballot chaser like me for one full day. That's about 75 doors and 25 real conversations with voters who haven't made up their minds yet, and who deserve to hear from us before it's too late. Every few months you start hearing political campaigns talk about another major fundraising deadline.
If you aren't living and breathing politics every day, it's completely fair to wonder: _What is all the noise actually about?_
Here is what it means: At the end of each quarter, federal campaigns are legally required to publicly report how much money they've raised and how much cash they have in the bank.
Those numbers become public for everyone to see -- reporters, political pundits, our opponents, and folks all across New Hampshire.
It's one of the rare moments when everyone has to put their cards on the table.
**While these reports don 't automatically win elections, they do tell us who has the momentum.**
Campaigns aren't built overnight. The resources we raise today are exactly what allow us to organize across the state, hire staff, and build the kind of grassroots operation it takes to win.
_That is especially true in a high-stakes race like ours._
New Hampshire is one of a handful of purple states that will determine control of the Senate. Outside groups and dark money-funded super PACs are already spending _millions_ trying to flip this seat, and the attacks aren't going to slow down.
The question is whether we will have the support we need to fight back -- and whether we can continue building a campaign powered by everyday people, not corporate interests.
**[That's why the upcoming end-of-quarter deadline on September 30th is so critical.](https://substack.com/redirect/ffc61d1b-d019-40fe-acef-c392e9dfc5c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[CHIP IN NOW](https://substack.com/redirect/ffc61d1b-d019-40fe-acef-c392e9dfc5c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This campaign isn't focused on the headlines, and it's certainly not focused on what political insiders in Washington think.
**This upcoming quarterly deadline matters because it 's our final one of this campaign -- and every single dollar represents someone who is choosing to stand with us in the remaining weeks of this race.**
Campaigns are strongest when they are built from the ground up. That's how I've run every race, and it's how we are going to win this one.
**[Chip in $5, $25, or whatever you can before this campaign's final end-of-quarter deadline on September 30th at midnight to help us keep this Senate seat blue and continue putting Granite Staters first.](https://substack.com/redirect/ffc61d1b-d019-40fe-acef-c392e9dfc5c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/ffc61d1b-d019-40fe-acef-c392e9dfc5c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I hope our fundraising numbers send a message that's impossible to miss:
This campaign is powered by people, not special interests -- and thousands of folks are coming together because they believe we can get things done and make a difference.
Thank you for being on this team,
Chris

body:
This week is absolutely critical.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
**The voter registration deadline in Texas is only _one week_ away.**
The GOP is terrified that they’re going to lose ground in Texas this year.
That’s why they’re trying to suppress voters to ensure a Republican win: In Tarrant County, 92 polling locations were shuttered, greatly reducing the accessibility of voting in the county. Then, millions of names were added to a voter suspense list, causing confusion in an attempt to discourage people from voting.
Our team is not taking this lying down. We refuse to let voters be discouraged from turning out and voting in this election. **That’s why it is absolutely critical to register as many voters as possible _this week_ before the voter registration deadline on October 5.**

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: Election help
body:
It's almost the end of March, and that means if you're anything like me you're seeing non-stop requests for money from political campaigns and organizations. And as you have likely seen, there are some striking similarities in these emails and the tactics they use:

There's the 3x match!
There's the 3x match!

Photos of Elissa's email inbox with 3x match requests
The 5x match!

Photos of Elissa's email inbox with 5x match requests
And even the 10x match!

Photos of Elissa's email inbox with 10x match requests
Here's the thing: none of that is real. No one is matching donations. They are trying to trick people into donating. It's cynical, and it's something we're never going to do here.

But we do have very real March fundraising goals. And right now, we are very much behind where we need to be with time running out.

Almost all of the donations our campaign receives comes from people giving smaller donations — often in response to emails like this one. But that means we have to ask.

And while I don't expect you to donate to every email we send, I hope that you will contribute to this one. It's an important time for our campaign, as we approach our first FEC fundraising deadline of the election year.

With all that in mind, can you please use this link to contribute whatever you can afford today? There's no matching donation, no super-donor ready to 10x your contribution—but it will help ensure we win this Senate race in Michigan and probably the presidential campaign in the state, as well.

CONTRIBUTE: https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/2455?t=1001&akid=2509%2E135344%2Eb5j8fV

Thank you,

Elissa Slotkin

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.elissaslotkin.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=2509%2E135344%2Eb5j8fV

| | Dear Peter,

I hope you’re doing well and enjoying the first few days of fall!

Before I get into why I’m writing today, I first wanted to extend a big thank you to everyone who responded to Valerie’s email last Monday about my birthday. I really appreciate those of you who either contributed or even dropped me a line to wish me well. It really meant a lot to me!

Today, I just wanted to drop you a quick note to let you know that this coming Wednesday is the deadline for [contributions](https://us.list-manage.com/YODvSMz3gv9?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) to appear on the next financial report in my campaign for re-election as Nevada Controller. This will be the final report before the election, which makes it a big one!

As I’ve mentioned before, every single dollar we raise from here on out will go directly into my voter-contact effort.

[You can contribute by clicking here.](https://us.list-manage.com/GnDYDHG9hgP?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)

Oh, and in case you missed it, [here is the TV ad](https://us.list-manage.com/KpOvxYRBVIu?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73) we’ve been running for a couple weeks now. We’ve been getting a great response, and your support today will help ensure we get that message in front of the voters who are going to determine the outcome of this election!

If you’ve contributed just recently, then please simply accept my sincerest thanks for your support. But if you haven’t had the chance to, then I hope I can count on you before Wednesday’s deadline.

Thank you so much, and God bless you!

For Nevada’s future,

Andy

body:
| Peter,

If you turn on your TV, you might see an ad from one of the 24 different corporate super PACs running ads for Miller-Meeks. She talks a lot about taking on the insurance lobby, big pharma, and tackling the cost-of-living crisis.

**I can't see how she'll do that, though, especially since she's taken over $300,000 from the big insurance industries & big pharma, and votes their way every single time.** Miller-Meeks has also voted for her party bosses' tariffs eight times — all while Iowans can barely afford groceries.

It's convenient for her. She goes to bat for her top donors and D.C. insiders — they pay her bills and first-class plane tickets and make sure she stays in power, all so she can remain their top spokesperson in Congress. **But who steps up to the plate for _the people of Iowa's 1st District?_** Right now, no one. Our district is being neglected by a self-serving politician, and I can't stand by and let it happen for another two years.

**I'm running to unseat Miller-Meeks and go to Washington to fight for my neighbors. But I can't win without you, Peter. Wild daisies surge past my waist, an unruly riot. Stems bend beneath the weight of neglected blooms; roots grip soil I have not had time to turn. The kitchen table remains no different: papers spread wide, grievances piled high, solutions buried deep. There is no paved path through this ground. We clear it by hand--one stone, one root, one hard question at a time. While others inherit roads already laid, we draw from the quiet of the soil to meet the heavy weight of discovery. Because a man is worth his hire, we earn the right to stand by doing the work. Representation is the manual labor of the unscripted.
**Pause.
Breath.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

Peter, this deadline matters more than most

| | Dear Peter,
Thank you. Whether you've donated, knocked on a door, shared a post, or simply believed in what we're building together, you are the reason this campaign is strong. I don't take a single bit of that for granted.
Today I'm reaching out because we've reached a moment that will shape the rest of this race, and I need your help.
**Our quarterly reporting deadline is Wednesday, September 30, at midnight, and we need to raise $6,000 before it closes.**
Here's why this deadline matters so much:
* **It keeps our digital ads running.** In the final stretch, our ads are how we reach thousands of voters in Butler, Preble, Darke, and Mercer Counties who haven't heard our message yet. Every dollar you give helps us meet people where they are, on their phones and in their feeds.
* **It keeps us on the Democratic slate card.** The slate card is one of the most trusted tools voters use when they head to the polls. We must meet our fundraising commitment to keep our place on it. Losing that spot would make it harder for voters to find us at the exact moment they're making their decision.

**Here's how we get there, together:** ✅ **60 people giving $100** , or
✅ **100 people giving $60**
That's it. That's all it takes. When neighbors come together, big goals become very reachable.****
---
| [DONATE $100 NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/i2Veey9Zi40?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)

| |

#### 🗳️ Voting begins one week from tomorrow: Tuesday, October 6
Early voting starts in just eight days. From that moment on, every conversation with a voter counts, and nothing persuades a voter like a neighbor at the door.
**We need volunteers to canvass on weekdays and weekends.** You don't need experience. We'll train you, pair you with a friendly team, and give you everything you need. One shift, even just two or three hours, can reach dozens of voters.
---
| [SIGN UP TO CANVASS ](https://us.list-manage.com/4c4wNA3Uv6C?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)

This campaign has always been about people, about families who deserve an economy that works for them, communities that deserve investment, and a representative who shows up and listens. You make that vision possible.
If you can give, please give today. If you can walk, please sign up to canvass. And if you can do both, you'll be helping us finish this race strong.
With deep gratitude and hope,
**Dr. Vanessa Enoch**
Democratic Nominee for Congress, Ohio's 8th District

# **Ivey League students sing "from the river to the sea" at AOC town hall event**

Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's "Students vs. Billionaires" event in Ithaca, part of her push to boost Democratic turnout ahead of November.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/369ea6f3-0bf8-40f0-996e-c595e8f192c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Petrova said:** "Cornell is fundamentally a capitalist institution that prioritizes billionaires and profit over students and community and is controlled by CEO trustees that are profiting off of genocide and war."

* **Ocasio-Cortez, touring upstate New York amid speculation about a 2028 presidential or Senate bid, accused Cornell of cracking down on student protesters:** "Whether it's the issue about Palestine or many others. Whether it's about people trying to fire those who are forming a union in their workplace, whether it's people trying to speak up about a number of different issues, we have to respond to that first crackdown," she said.
* **Gov. Kathy Hochul backed out of a planned joint appearance with Ocasio-Cortez** that day. Her office cited the nor'easter hitting New York City, though Hochul had no public events scheduled Sunday.

Speaking in Metz on the last day of his four-day France visit, Pope Leo XIV said Europe **[cannot be discussed without Christianity](https://substack.com/redirect/13359cda-aa0d-407f-a110-4e01dbb837c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , while praising European integration as a "social and political necessity" and urging EU leaders to give real substance to ideals like freedom, democracy, and unity.
[| | | | | Catholic Arena
---
@CatholicArena
🚨 The Champs Elysee is completely FULL This is unbelievable The people have France have turned out in their hundreds of thousands to see Pope Leo XIV, the atmosphere is electric
| 12:20 PM * Sep 26, 2026 * 3.91M Views376 Replies * 4.94K Reposts * 33.9K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/a7d7fe6f-3b72-437c-81cf-b7d644ce030b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Leo told an interfaith audience that Europe thrives by reinventing its past** through encounters with others. The day before, at Lourdes, he condemned France's new assisted-dying law as "false compassion" and called the sick the "beating heart of our humanity."
* **Crowds have been massive, including 800,000 at a Paris Mass,** and adult and teen baptisms in France are up 20% over last year. Leo closes the trip with Mass at Metz's Gothic cathedral, known for its Chagall-designed stained glass.

* * *
# **ICE reportedly halts arrests of non-criminals; DHS disputes it**
ICE officers nationwide were told over the weekend to arrest only illegal immigrants with criminal convictions or charges beyond illegal entry, **[sources told The Daily Wire.](https://substack.com/redirect/e310663a-06a4-471f-b1f0-007cfa33c430?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** People with final deportation orders but no criminal record would be spared, and "collateral arrests" of others found near a target would end.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e310663a-06a4-471f-b1f0-007cfa33c430?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **DHS called the claims "false," saying "no one is off the table"** and pointing to a new enforcement surge in sanctuary cities focused on violent offenders. Sources suggested the shift could be aimed at calming tensions before the midterms, as Trump's immigration approval has slipped to 43% from 48%.
* **The report follows an ICE shooting in Austin last weekend involving an officer not wearing a body camera,** and leadership comolications after the White House pulled Mullin's pick to lead ICE. Sources also cited a similar July pause on traffic stops that Trump reversed.

* * *
# **SpaceX Starship reaches orbit for first time despite engine loss**
SpaceX's Starship **[lifted off from Texas Monday](https://substack.com/redirect/0a074cc6-9de1-415b-9e74-d16a821c93cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on its 14th test flight, its first attempt to reach orbit. The rocket lost an engine minutes after launch, but controllers cleared it to continue, and a single Raptor engine completed the orbital burn about 26 minutes in.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0a074cc6-9de1-415b-9e74-d16a821c93cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **The roughly 10-hour uncrewed mission aims to circle Earth six times and deploy 26 Starlink satellites** before splashing down in the Pacific west of Chile. Its booster completed a simulated landing burn and splashed down off the Texas coast.
* **Earlier flights were suborbital and ended in splashdowns about an hour after liftoff.** NASA plans to use a future Starship as a crewed lunar lander, while SpaceX's longer-term goal is a fleet carrying humans to Mars.

They show you who bought in, how much they gave, and who might expect their call answered the next time that member of Congress takes a big vote.
It's all there in black and white, and once you see what's gone into some campaigns, you might lose your appetite. Frankly, most of Congress ought to come with a warning label for all the corporate PAC checks and industry money packed into their campaigns.

Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

#
Peter, over the weekend, _The New York Times_ released a profile of VoteVets and the work we’ve done this cycle. Inside, there are some numbers we wanted to make sure you saw.
$9.7 million.
That’s the amount we put into Iowa behind Josh Turek’s US Senate primary campaign.
$4.5 million.
That’s the amount we’re putting into Iowa to make sure Josh Turek defeats Ashley Hinson in the general election.
Six.
That’s the amount of times Ashley Hinson voted against War Powers Resolutions that could have stopped the Iran War, before she called for an immediate end to it last week.
$60 million.
That’s how much we’re spending nationwide on elections this year.
331\.
That’s the number of Democratic candidates we are backing in those elections.
20\.
That’s the number of US House and Senate races, and...
311\.
That’s the number of down-ballot races we’re supporting. And Peter, that’s the number we want you to think about.
The federal races are the ones that get the most attention. Everyone is invested in what races could flip the House and Senate this year, and we imagine you’re no different. VoteVets candidates will be the difference between a Democratic and Republican Congress in 2027.
But it is those 311 down-ballot races that are the real story. Those are 311 leaders of principle from military families, national security backgrounds, or the armed forces of the United States. Democrats at all levels of government.
Those 311 candidates are the future. And it is support from you that makes that future possible. So, here’s one more number:
$5.

**From _The New York Times:_ Supreme Court Allows Federal Voter Identification Tool Ahead of Midterms **
* * *
Folks, this is serious. **The Supreme Court just cleared the way for the Trump administration to combine your personal data – including citizenship information and Social Security numbers – into a nationwide voter database to determine if you’re an eligible, lawful voter.** A federal judge already found that the agencies behind this system **“haphazardly combined and repurposed the private information of millions of Americans, including citizenship data that they knew to be unreliable.”** Now states can run their voter rolls through it before November. In her dissent, Justice Jackson warned the ruling could lead states to cancel the registrations of recently naturalized citizens or force them to prove their citizenship before voting. Recently the Republican Town Committee of Fairfield, Ct. raised the issue of repeated flooding episodes on the Rooster River.
Thanks for reading The Goldstein Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..BSUMcWxx3K9pEwbENVv47MBlY6eGjQs-qa49kwC1bfs?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=217842988)
Relief has been promised since 2003 but has never been delivered. The State of Connecticut was supposed to provide $42 million through bonding, which still has not happened.
The project was put out to bid to build the flood mitigation structures on the Fairfield Wheeler Golf Course. The bidding is closed but without funding this project seems to be in limbo.
The flooding also affects Bridgeport residents.
What is amazing is that it does not appear that Connecticut has even bothered to seek Federal funds to help pay for the project. In fact the Federal government, if they approved the project would pay up to 75% of the cost. Towns cannot solicit Federal funds under these programs the State of Connecticut must apply for the funds for the benefit of the project.
The following is a list of Federal Departments and Agencies that fund flood mitigation: the Department of Agriculture, The Environmental Protection Agency, FEMA, The Army Corps of Engineers, The Mitigation Section of the National Flood Insurance Act and probably other agencies.
Since there are multiple Federal agencies that provide flood insurance and have to pay the claims for damages it makes sense that these agencies do provide funding for flood mitigation. In the long run it is less expensive to prevent problems then to have to constantly pay to repair homes that are repeatedly damaged.
The State of Connecticut has failed the flood victims on the Rooster River. They have also failed the Taxpayers of Connecticut by not seeking Federal funds to pay for flood remediation.
No wonder we have among the highest taxes in the US.
It is time for people to wake up and understand that one party rule by the Democrat party at the State and Federal Level does not work.
I am running for Congress because I feel that the Democrats who represent us at both the Federal and State level are not representing the interests of the people of the State of Connecticut.
This failure to solve this recurring flooding problem is just an example of why we need change.
Roosters are known for waking people up. Maybe the problems with the Rooster River will do the same.

name: Violet at Swing Left
subject: Why this work is important to me
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
Support these Swing Left Fellows at the next Weekend of Action.
#
Hi there, I’m Violet, an Organizing Manager for Swing Left, and I’m proud to lead our College Fellows Program.
College students are eager to organize, but they often lack the funding and specialized training required for effective fieldwork. **We built the College Fellows Program to bridge that exact gap, providing hands-on training in recruitment, organizing skills, and event logistics.**
This work is deeply personal to me. Just two and a half years ago, I was in these students' shoes as a campus organizer. I was only able to succeed because of really good mentors who invested in me and gave me the resources I needed to learn how to organize effectively. I still credit that experience for getting me to where I am today.
Now I get to provide that same kind of support to students just getting started through Swing Left’s College Fellows Program.
Today, college groups make up _nearly one-fourth of Swing Left’s entire national network_ , and it’s so exciting to see what students do once they have the tools and support to organize.
These students are both creative and tenacious in their recruitment: One of our fellows recently told me she recruited campus acapella groups to sing at their canvass launch. Other students who have never knocked on a single door before are now taking on their first canvassing shifts while also training their peers to do the same.
This weekend, our 37 College Fellows are putting their skills to work as they help to organize Ground Truth canvasses across the country as part of our next nationwide Weekend of Action on Saturday, October 3rd and Sunday, October 4th. They span 21 schools in states across the country. And thanks to Donuts and Democracy, fellows across the country will also have donuts waiting for volunteers at their canvasses! It’s a great example of the community that’s growing around these students and the work they are leading.
**The support this community has given Swing Left is what makes programs like the College Fellows possible. It gives students the training, mentorship, and resources to become organizers, and a chance to put those skills to work reaching thousands of voters in critical swing districts and states. This weekend, you can be a part of what they’ve helped build:**
[**You can be a part of what they’ve helped build by signing up to join Ground Truth volunteers at a canvassing event near you.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/1218?utm_source=em20260928-2945&t=3&akid=2945%2E1562180%2ERoWs0a)
Thank you for being part of this community. I hope to see you on the doors this fall!
Violet K
Organizing Manager, Swing Left

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. In most states, the lieutenant governor is a largely ceremonial position. **In Texas,****that couldn’t be further from the truth. ** **The Texas Lt. Governor controls** the entire Texas Senate — setting the agenda, appointing committee chairs, deciding which bills live and which ones die. _It is one of the most powerful positions in state government in America._ Dan Patrick has held it for over a decade, and he has used every bit of that power:
* **_To push book bans and keep parents and educators fighting culture wars instead of fixing underfunded schools.

_**
* **_To drain money from public schools by forcing through the billion-dollar voucher scheme.

_**
* **_To hand out BILLIONS in taxpayer incentives to AI data center companies...the same companies whose investors have poured millions into his campaign._**

Before Ken Paxton’s impeachment trial began, a pro-Paxton political group gave Dan Patrick $1 million and loaned it another $2 million. Patrick presided over the trial, and lo and behold! Paxton was acquitted. **This is the system of corruption that has become the norm under Dan Patrick.** When I sat down with Velshi, I made the case that what happens in the Texas Lt. Governor's office doesn't stay in Texas. Water policy, school funding, energy infrastructure, reproductive rights — these are decided by whoever controls the Texas Senate calendar. And the decisions we make impact the whole nation. I'm running to change the trajectory of our state, and our country. To put the power back in the hands of the people. And to fight for every Texan. For Texas, Rep. Vikki Goodwin

Peter, I don’t like receiving these emails as much as the next guy, but with Election Day less than 40 days away and America’s future on the line, I’m left without a choice.
I spent a lot of time writing this, so please read each word carefully.
It’s Kellyanne Conway: I’m a pollster by trade, so I can sniff out phony polls from a mile away. When I saw these numbers, it had me genuinely worried:
---
| VIRGINIA’S 2ND CONGRESSIONAL DISTRICT POLLING
---
JEN KIGGANS (R) | ELAINE LURIA (D)
47%| 47%
| [HELP JEN PULL AHEAD](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.-89MQ)
---
VA-02 is one of the REAL toss-up races in America, and the decision you make today could have a massive impact this November.
Losing Jen Kiggans would spell disaster for our Conservative House Majority and our country.
Jen is a Navy Veteran who flew H-46 and H-3 helicopters and completed two deployments to the Persian Gulf. After her service, Jen became a board-certified Nurse Practitioner and continued to serve in long-term care and nursing facilities in Virginia Beach and Norfolk. Her entire life has been dedicated to service.
---
[](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._w6JQ2Dxk4oP3g)
---
Jen got in this fight because she saw how Democrats and Joe Biden crippled America with their far-left policies and knew she had to get involved. She made a massive leap of faith in 2022, when she flipped a blue seat red and immediately got to work.
Now, the same Democrat Jen ousted in 2022 is back for revenge – and her opponent has the backing of the entire Democrat Establishment and their money machine.
With the rise of the DSA and socialists, I’m extremely worried if Democrats win this seat. If they do, they will be even closer to flipping the House, and will immediately move to:

* Gut border security and open the southern border back up
* Defund ICE
* Raise our taxes
* Usher in DEI in our schools, military, and at every level of government
* Impeach President Trump

Peter, we cannot rest on our laurels for another second. [I’m launching a 24-hour fundraising blitz to help Jen reach her MOST important goal of the year and propel her to victory.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.)
---
| [MAGA BLITZ ACTIVATED](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._JOF-3ZfVE_Ep_Gzmw)
---
| [GIVE ANY AMOUNT](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.)
---
We have a real chance here at tipping the scales back in our favor, but it requires every Conservative reading this to step up and do their part.
I hope I can count on you today.
Talk soon,
Kellyanne Conway
