subject: A huge development in this Senate race
body:
What just happened in North Carolina.
---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-cooper-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260928_9446_fr&refcode2=9446_22930333_ZKKl6k&akid=9446%2E22930333%2EZKKl6k)
---
This news changes everything, Derek. Let me explain.
As I write this, the GOP is going all in to defeat me. President Trump has endorsed my MAGA opponent and personally attacked me on social media, Stephen Miller went on Fox News to rant and rave about me and dark-money groups are putting millions behind baseless ads lying about who I am and what I’m fighting for.
Republicans are coming after me so hard because experts say that if we lose here in North Carolina, Democrats will lose our chance at taking back the Senate.
Unfortunately, these attacks are making an impact – a recent poll of this race shows us statistically tied – and the GOP is continuing to strike while the iron’s hot.
**In July, the Senate GOP's top super PAC launched brand-new TV ads all across the state.** They’re ramping up their efforts to defeat me earlier than expected, and now, they’re spending more in North Carolina than almost any other battleground in the country.
**I need your help, Derek. We’re getting outspent, and without your immediate grassroots support before our critical end-of-quarter deadline, we could put our shot at flipping this seat at risk.** [**If you care about winning in North Carolina and retaking the Senate, making a well-timed donation of $20 split between our campaign and the DNC is the best thing you can do to help me fight back and win. Hi there, Peter – Roy again.
By now, you’ve likely gotten a barrage of texts and emails – from myself included – about the upcoming "FEC end-of-quarter deadline" this Wednesday. I get it. I know it can start to feel like just another reason to ask for money. That’s why I want to take a moment to explain what this deadline means, and why it’s different.
[**_If you already know why it matters for our team though, I hope you’ll consider chipping in a few bucks to my grassroots campaign before you click away._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1447&amount=5&t=8&akid=3886%2E124072%2E677L_I)

Every three months, campaigns are legally required to publicly report their fundraising numbers. The report is available to everyone: journalists, supporters and opponents – and they will be watching. It’s a key indicator of where a race stands, and a strong showing carries real weight for any campaign.
**So it’s not an exaggeration to say that this quarterly FEC deadline (the last of its kind before the election) will be the biggest test yet of our grassroots strength.**
Peter, North Carolina hasn’t sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 2008, but any chance we have of taking back the majority this fall depends on our winning. The GOP knows as well as I do that we have the momentum to do it – _but they have the money_ , and they’re spending more than $100 million of it just to defeat me.
That’s _$100 million_ to flood the airwaves with lies about me and my record, as they throw even more MAGA rallies with President Trump and buy his handpicked candidate Michael Whatley’s way to victory.
**If they detect any weakness in our numbers, it’ll give them incentive to spend tens of millions more to drown us out entirely in these final weeks.**
That’s a risk we can’t afford so late in the race. We have to show everyone that our grassroots movement is thriving and unstoppable – that we have what it takes to build the strongest voter outreach and mobilization program our state has ever seen.
[**_We need to dig deep, Peter, so if you’re able to make a contribution today, it would mean the world to me and my campaign. Every dollar will be put to work immediately to stay one step ahead of the GOP, reach the voters we need to flip this seat and return power in Washington to where it belongs: in the hands of working people._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1447&amount=5&t=13&akid=3886%2E124072%2E677L_I)

Roy Cooper

# Iran
* **Trump expects more Iran talks:** President Donald Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/ce9d8b1a-b512-47b6-b98f-a4fc76700518?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he expects further U.S.-Iran talks this week, one day after rejecting Tehran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear negotiations.
* "They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make," Trump told Axios, adding when asked about renewed U.S. strikes: "I am always thinking about it."
* U.S. Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said Washington rejected Iran's proposal because it sought access to billions of dollars in frozen Iranian funds and the lifting of sanctions, also citing concerns over Iran's nuclear program. Iran is "asking for everything up front," he said.
* Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [said](https://substack.com/redirect/69cf3f0f-5a87-4911-b24f-a46a476b01c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Tehran remains ready for "real diplomacy," but is also prepared for renewed war. "We came to forge peace," Araghchi said, adding that Iran would remain steadfast against aggression "even if it comes to an apocalyptic war."
* Qatari mediators have continued shuttle diplomacy and presented both sides with a compromise proposal, with regional sources telling Axios another round of indirect dialogue could take place as early as Monday.
* A source close to Iran's UN delegation, however, [told](https://substack.com/redirect/fa005d71-2ba1-41c2-8d19-36ce5f415ad1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) IRNA that no new round of negotiations is currently scheduled and that Tehran is awaiting a U.S. response through Qatari mediators.
* **Iran files ICAO complaint over U.S. flight restrictions:** Iran [filed](https://substack.com/redirect/ff61a383-8d95-41e2-9c19-162ecce1408c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a formal complaint with the International Civil Aviation Organization over U.S. flight restrictions and is pursuing the restoration of routes suspended by several countries.
* Iran's CAO chief told state media Iran is working through diplomatic and legal channels to restore flights, including to Baghdad and Najaf, with Najaf expected to resume services "in the coming days."
* The U.S. sanctioned 27 Iranian airlines on September 8 and threatened secondary sanctions against airports and companies providing Iranian aircraft with fuel, landing services or ticket sales. Oman and the UAE have since suspended Iranian flights, while four Iraqi airports have halted them.
* Iraq's ambassador to Iran [said](https://substack.com/redirect/e1a81402-88a4-4cf2-abc9-176756039c53?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Monday that Najaf airport would resume Iranian flights within 24 hours, adding that Iraq had not ordered flights suspended but foreign ground-service companies had stopped servicing Iranian aircraft.
* **Eight U.S. Marines injured in previously undisclosed Iranian missile attack in Strait of Hormuz:** Eight U.S. Marines were [injured](https://substack.com/redirect/79001e9f-ffb1-4503-855b-59d825d1e5d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in an Iranian anti-ship cruise missile attack on a vessel they were operating aboard in the Strait of Hormuz on September 14, NBC reported.
* The Marines suffered smoke inhalation and possible traumatic brain injuries, including concussion symptoms such as headaches, but returned to duty soon afterward. Officials declined to identify the type of vessel involved but said it was not a U.S. Navy ship.
* The Pentagon's Defense Casualty Analysis System added the eight Marines to its casualty count nearly ten days after the attack. The database now records 861 U.S. service members injured in the war with Iran.
* Iran [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/39064ae4-1107-409b-a8ea-0af6073e7133?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it struck 19 ships in the Strait of Hormuz over the past two nights. Iranian officials said any ship crossing without authorization will face an armed response.
* **Five arrested near UK airbase used for U.S. strikes on Iran:** Five men were arrested on suspicion of preparing a "terrorist" act near RAF Fairford, a military airbase in western England used by U.S. forces to launch attacks on Iran. Armed police made the arrests early Sunday after receiving reports of three suspicious vehicles apparently heading toward the base.
* President Donald Trump claimed the suspects intended to do "big damage" and said British and U.S. authorities were investigating.
* Police have not identified a suspected motive or said who they believe was involved, and no charges have been filed.
* Asked whether Iran could be involved, UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting [said](https://substack.com/redirect/8a0723e4-894b-431c-a459-3b5c43c6eadd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it would be "very unwise" to speculate. The Iranian Embassy in the UK "categorically rejects and strongly condemns" speculation linking Iran to the incident.
* **IRGC claims seizure of U.S. underwater vehicle in Hormuz:** The IRGC Navy [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/39743c8b-2e01-400e-9533-161c596b79de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it seized a second unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) in the Strait of Hormuz "through a coordinated and complex operation involving intelligence superiority and electronic warfare."
* Iran identified it as a U.S. Navy's MK18 Mod 2 Kingfish, which is primarily designed for mine clearance. The U.S. military rejected Tehran's claim.
* **Middle East oil exports rebound as Saudi shipments surge:** Crude exports from major Middle Eastern producers are on track to reach 12.8 million barrels per day (bpd) in September, their highest level since the U.S.-Israel war with Iran began, according to [Kpler data](https://substack.com/redirect/c94ffc18-969b-471b-8eb6-d50daff27e13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* The rebound was driven by increased Saudi and UAE shipments and a recovery in flows through the Strait of Hormuz, though exports remain well below February's 18.8 million bpd.
* Saudi exports are expected to reach about 5.4 million bpd this month, up from 2.45 million in August, as the kingdom diverted shipments from the Red Sea port of Yanbu following attacks on its East-West pipeline.
* Despite these rosy export projections, [prices for oil remain near their highs](https://substack.com/redirect/edfa0d43-657c-4367-8cc5-87c77f320997?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* U.S. Treasury yields hit new post-financial crisis highs on both the [10-year ](https://substack.com/redirect/03f75faf-df8f-4a44-8466-390315d7593f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)and [30-year note](https://substack.com/redirect/6b21a593-4c17-4c60-8dc9-cc0cf4386567?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as mortgage rates climbed above 7%.
* **Pezeshkian brings tons of pharmaceutical supplies from India as Iran faces medicine shortages:** President Masoud Pezeshkian [used](https://substack.com/redirect/da9583d2-117b-4c4e-b59e-b5da47d74156?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his visit to India for the BRICS summit this month to transport several tons of pharmaceutical ingredients back to Iran on his private plane, The Financial Times reported.

# Yemen
* **Seven killed, 40 injured in Saudi strike on Taiz:** Seven people were killed and 40 others, including children, in a [strike](https://substack.com/redirect/4f824c89-99d8-4262-bdf3-6aeb36ea0b09?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the Mawiya junction in Yemen's Taiz province on Sunday. The Ansarallah Health Ministry said Saudi airstrikes hit commercial shops at the market.
* Yemen's Saudi-backed government claimed its own forces targeted an Ansarallah military camp and vehicles at Mawiya.
* 164 people were killed and 645 injured in Yemen between September 19 and 26, according to the World Health Organization. Since August 6, WHO has documented 838 deaths among 4,481 casualties. Fighting has also displaced more than 180,000 people.
* **EU 's Kallas calls for more ships for Red Sea mission as Ansarallah expand control: **EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called on member states to provide more ships to the bloc's Aspides naval mission to protect Red Sea shipping, saying she has pushed for reinforcements but received no firm commitments.
* The EU launched Aspides in February 2024 to protect commercial vessels from attacks in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and surrounding waters.
* Recent territorial advances have left Ansarallah positioned around 20 kilometers from the African coast and with effective control over the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, four Palestinians were killed and 19 injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,022 killed, with 175,980 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,421 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,983, while 834 bodies have been recovered.

* **Israeli strike kills woman, wounds several others in Gaza City:** An Israeli airstrike [targeted](https://substack.com/redirect/af539d87-3816-478f-88d8-de4dcd41b2b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a home that was sheltering displaced Palestinians in northern Gaza City, according to WAFA, killing a Palestinian woman and wounding several others.
* **Israeli settlers attack Palestinian olive harvest amid occupied West Bank closure:** Israeli authorities imposed a week-long closure across the occupied West Bank on Sunday, tightening restrictions at checkpoints and military barriers, citing Jewish holidays.
* **Ramallah and Al-Bireh:** Settlers [stole](https://substack.com/redirect/32ce60c9-0bfe-4bc6-b945-92da4ab79b06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) olives from Palestinian land in Sinjil, Turmus Ayya and Umm Safa, while others set fire to a Palestinian-owned vehicle in Deir Abu Mashal.
* The attacks come as the olive harvest begins, a period during which Palestinian farmers frequently face attacks on their trees, crops, and access to agricultural land.
* **Jenin:** Settlers entered agricultural land in Khirbet Masoud with tractors and stole harvested olives, according to WAFA.
* **Nablus:** Israeli settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/52f39a26-cb0d-4f95-8a00-cb4bb5c5dddf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a 75-year-old Palestinian man while he was on his land in Sebastia, northwest of Nablus, beating him and pouring boiling water on his body, WAFA reported.
* **Hebron:** Israeli forces [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/8bbd357c-a69f-49c8-bd3d-7b3f4dac657f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the town of Al-Samu and the Bir Haram Al-Rama area of Hebron alongside settlers. In Masafer Yatta, settlers cut and stole electricity cables.
* **Katz, Ben-Gvir lead over 1,270 Israelis into Al-Aqsa Mosque compound:** Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir [led](https://substack.com/redirect/2731465e-dc94-48d3-85d3-7e8baaf60b66?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at least 1,271 Israelis into the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound on Monday, on the third day of the Jewish holiday of Sukkot. Groups performed religious rituals under heavy Israeli police protection.
* **Israeli settlers attack home of Palestinian-American in the occupied West Bank:** Israeli settlers attacked the home of 78-year-old Palestinian-American Mustafa Zaater and his wife on Sunday in Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, setting fire to three of his vehicles, smashing doors and windows, and attempting to enter the house.
* Zaater told Drop Site contributor Mutasem Sqf ElHait that dozens of settlers, some carrying weapons, approached from the northern and southern sides of the area at around 1:30 a.m.
* "They want to drive us out of here," Zaater said. "This is our land and our property. We're not going to give it to them and leave."
* Residents eventually pushed the settlers back, Abu Falah village council member Omar Hamayel, adding that Israeli forces fired tear gas at them after the settlers had withdrawn.**Watch Sqf ElHait 's dispatch [here](https://substack.com/redirect/f48f546b-4f8e-421a-a0c5-be04c84af305?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
* **Ben-Gvir threatens Palestinian prisoner with execution:** Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir published [footage](https://substack.com/redirect/b0e95561-1365-43b8-bdff-90cebefc22b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Sunday showing him inside the prison cell of Palestinian prisoner Hassan Salama, telling him: "I want to kill you. ... I want you executed."
* Salama, 55, has been imprisoned since 1996 and is serving 48 life sentences over his alleged role in a series of Hamas-orchestrated attacks. He has spent a total of more than 14 years in solitary confinement.
* The Palestinian Prisoners' Society condemned Ben-Gvir's threat, saying it reflected a broader Israeli policy rather than an isolated act and warning that such public threats could precede attempts to kill Palestinian prisoner leaders.
* **Netanyahu secretly visited UAE, asked president to deny report he warned him before October 7 attack:** Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu [secretly traveled](https://substack.com/redirect/5f78d31a-2dde-4145-be3c-fc20186bd3b3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the UAE on Sunday for a meeting with President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, two people briefed on the trip told the Associated Press.
* The meeting focused on a Haaretz report that Sheikh Mohamed had warned Netanyahu of a looming Hamas attack shortly before October 7, 2023. Netanyahu asked the Emirati president to publicly deny the report, a source with firsthand knowledge of the meeting told the AP. Netanyahu's office has denied receiving such a warning.
* **Israel revokes status of Dutch diplomats over settlement goods ban:** Israel revoked the status of diplomats representing the Netherlands in Ramallah, giving them seven days to return their Israeli-issued diplomatic documents, in response to Dutch measures targeting Israeli settlements.

# Lebanon
* **Israeli airstrike hits southern Lebanon as ceasefire violations continue:** Israeli warplanes [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/3d2e20a1-0e15-4d35-bd7e-6937435ac024?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an airstrike on Monday between the towns of Mayfadoun and Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah in southern Lebanon's Nabatieh governorate, while Israeli artillery targeted the outskirts of Zibqin and valleys near Yater, according to Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA).
* **Hezbollah chief calls for halt to direct Israel talks, says disarmament must follow Israeli withdrawal:** Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem called Sunday for Lebanon to freeze direct negotiations with Israel and return to "indirect" talks, while saying Hezbollah is prepared to discuss the state's monopoly on weapons only after Israel withdraws from Lebanese territory.
* Qassem called the U.S.-sponsored Framework Agreement a "shameful concession of all the cards" Lebanon could use to secure its rights and accused the government of "helping the Israeli-American project instead of confronting it." He said the president has the right to negotiate, but not to "give up Lebanon's right to defend its land."
* Qassem said Hezbollah is "ready for dialogue and discussion" over its weapons but insisted the "liberation of the south" must come first. Qassem also pledged Hezbollah would contribute to shelter and reconstruction efforts in southern Lebanon and said it would soon announce its participation in a housing project.

# Other International News
* **Myanmar military airstrike kills at least 33 people in Rakhine state:** At least 33 people were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/7ab2d6b5-cfcf-4470-9e46-6365fa883a73?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and 36 injured in a military airstrike near a market in Kyauktaw, a town in western Myanmar's Rakhine state controlled by the Arakan Army, according to the rebel group and a local aid worker.
* Local aid worker Wai Hun Aung said the strike hit an area "quite far from the fighting" and unrelated to active combat.
* The Arakan Army said the attack was among the deadliest airstrikes in Rakhine since a December 2025 strike on a hospital that killed at least 30 people.
* **Pro-government forces capture strategic Tigray town as Ethiopia fighting escalates:** Ethiopia's military and allied militias announced that they have [taken](https://substack.com/redirect/6bfd2bff-4408-4c99-9b8a-bf5ef1c0d76e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Alamata, a key supply hub about 120 km south of Tigray's capital Mekelle, Reuters [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/6bfd2bff-4408-4c99-9b8a-bf5ef1c0d76e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* The reported capture would reverse some of the gains made by Tigrayan forces after they launched a new offensive last week and comes amid the most serious fighting since the 2022 Pretoria peace agreement ended Ethiopia's devastating civil war.
* Ethiopia's military has accused Eritrea, Sudan's armed forces and Egypt of backing opposition forces. Internet and phone service in Tigray has also remained disrupted for several days.
* In separate fighting in the country this week Ethiopia's military said it inflicted heavy losses on Tigrayan forces during fighting in northern Amhara and Afar.

* **Serbia 's president Vučic resigns, positioning himself to return as prime minister**: President Aleksandar Vučic [stepped down](https://substack.com/redirect/8ba85be1-c362-4f42-b125-39d5b8c08792?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Sunday, seven months before his final term expired, allowing him to become prime minister if his Serbian Progressive Party forms a government after the October 25 snap parliamentary election.
* Parliamentary Speaker Ana Brnabić will serve as interim president, with a presidential vote to follow by December.
* The parliamentary election will pit Vučić's ruling bloc against Students Win, an anti-corruption movement, and the pro-Western European Serbia alliance.

* **South Korea summons Ukrainian envoy over disclosure of North Korean prisoner transfer** : South Korea summoned Ukraine's acting ambassador and demanded an explanation and apology after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy publicly revealed that two captured North Korean soldiers had been transferred from Ukraine to South Korea.
* Seoul said the disclosure violated a confidentiality agreement between the two governments and accused Ukraine's presidential office of falsely denying that such an agreement existed.
* Zelenskyy announced at the UN General Assembly that the two North Korean soldiers had been captured while fighting for Russia in Ukraine and were later transferred to South Korea.

* **France 's far-right National Rally expands Senate presence ahead of 2027 presidential election:** Marine Le Pen's National Rally and its allies [emerged](https://substack.com/redirect/b438800a-ddd7-47bc-b8fc-21551a7dac10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from Sunday's indirect elections with a record 14 seats in France's 348-member Senate, clearing the threshold to form an official parliamentary group for the first time.
* The result gives the far right additional resources and visibility as Le Pen prepares another presidential bid next year, when Emmanuel Macron leaves office.
* "The results have exceeded our expectations," Le Pen said, calling the outcome a "historic victory." National Rally first entered the Senate in 2014 with two seats.

* **Ukrainian strikes force fourth Russian refinery shutdown in under a week:** Ukrainian drones hit [another](https://substack.com/redirect/9437c966-c6d1-4399-9998-60e83d526e1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Russian refinery ablaze over the weekend, Reuters reported, as Kyiv's campaign disrupts Russian fuel exports.
* Before the strikes, Russia exported roughly 900,000 to 1 million barrels of diesel a day--about 10% of global supply. Kpler data now puts its net diesel exports near 100,000 barrels a day.
* Ukraine's General Staff said its forces also struck a missile-components plant in Azov operated by Russia's Tactical Missiles Corporation.
* Russia launched 173 drones overnight into Saturday and another 170 overnight into Sunday, with strikes recorded at 18 locations, according to Ukraine's air force. Attacks killed at least two people in Kyiv and the Odessa region overnight into Sunday, while Kyiv endured near-continuous attacks for a second consecutive day.

* **RSF commander defects to Sudanese army with 50 fighters:** A Rapid Support Forces commander, Al-Tayeb al-Wahidu, and 50 fighters defected to the Sudanese military in Omdurman, Drop Site's Godfrey Olukya [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/59b75d8a-168d-4437-8b1d-19054e3d85f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Sudanese army Major Ali Gubba said Saturday that the group arrived Friday in five trucks and was received by senior military and intelligence officials.
* Speaking to reporters, Wahidu attributed his departure to pervasive abuses within the RSF and urged other fighters to lay down their weapons and join the Sudanese armed forces.
* Gubba said many of the defectors belonged to the Mahamid clan, led by Musa Hilal, a former militia commander who split from the RSF and moved from North Darfur to government-held territory in February.

* **Final U.S. troops withdraw from Iraq amid Kurdish leaders warnings:** The last U.S. troops are [scheduled](https://substack.com/redirect/6e9d4a24-b0d4-422f-a9ef-310a614cfaa5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to leave Iraq by September 30, with Kurdistan Regional Government Prime Minister Masrour Barzani warning that the departure leaves the region exposed to Iranian retaliation. "The threat is real--we are vulnerable, we are being attacked," Barzani told the Financial Times, calling the prospect of being left without air defenses "shameful."
* At least 1,000 Iranian drones and missiles have targeted Iraqi Kurdistan since the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran began in February, according to the regional government, primarily targeting U.S. military sites and Iranian Kurdish opposition camps.
* The regional government says it has no air defenses of its own and that Baghdad controls their purchase. The State Department described the withdrawal as marking "an important page" in U.S.-Iraq relations.

Drop Site Daily: September 28, 2026 | | | Sep 28 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Israeli soldiers walk by a Palestinian vendor in the Old City market in occupied East Jerusalem. Photo by Nasser Ishtayeh/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images. Monday, September 28, 2026 - Iran: President Donald Trump expects more Iran talks. Iran files International Civil Aviation Organization complaint over U.S. flight restrictions. Eight U.S. Marines injured in previously undisclosed Iranian missile attack in Strait of Hormuz. Five arrested near UK airbase used for U.S. strikes on Iran. IRGC claims seizure of U.S. underwater vehicle in Hormuz. Middle East oil exports rebound as Saudi shipments surge. Yemen: Seven killed, 40 injured in Saudi strike on Taiz. EU's Kallas calls for more ships for Red Sea mission as Ansarallah expand control. Palestine: Israeli strike kills woman, wounds several others in Gaza City. Israeli settlers attack Palestinian olive harvest amid occupied West Bank closure. Israeli settlers attack home of Palestinian-American in the occupied West Bank. Ben-Gvir threatens Palestinian prisoner with execution. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secretly visited UAE, asked president to deny report he warned him before October 7 attack. Lebanon: Israeli airstrike hits southern Lebanon as ceasefire violations continue. Hezbollah chief calls for halt to direct Israel talks, says disarmament must follow Israeli withdrawal. U.S.: Troy Jackson defies consultants, denounces genocide in Gaza. Susan Collins bribery scandal mushrooming. New poll has Abdul El-Sayed leading Mike Rogers 48-44%, Trump badly underwater. Iowa Senate candidate Ashley Hinson reaches new levels of Iran war incoherence. New poll finds Darline Graham, Lindsey's sister, at risk of losing South Carolina Senate seat. International: Myanmar military airstrike kills at least 33 people in Rakhine state. Pro-government forces capture strategic Tigray town as Ethiopia fighting escalates. France's far-right National Rally expands Senate presence ahead of 2027 presidential election. Ukrainian strikes force fourth Russian refinery shutdown in under a week. RSF commander defects to Sudanese army with 50 fighters. Final U.S. troops withdraw from Iraq amid Kurdish leaders warnings. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Trump expects more Iran talks: President Donald Trump he expects further U.S.-Iran talks this week, one day after rejecting Tehran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear negotiations. "They want to make a deal, but it is not the deal that I want to make," Trump told Axios, adding when asked about renewed U.S. strikes: "I am always thinking about it." U.S. Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said Washington rejected Iran's proposal because it sought access to billions of dollars in frozen Iranian funds and the lifting of sanctions, also citing concerns over Iran's nuclear program. Iran is "asking for everything up front," he said. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi Tehran remains ready for "real diplomacy," but is also prepared for renewed war. "We came to forge peace," Araghchi said, adding that Iran would remain steadfast against aggression "even if it comes to an apocalyptic war." Qatari mediators have continued shuttle diplomacy and presented both sides with a compromise proposal, with regional sources telling Axios another round of indirect dialogue could take place as early as Monday. A source close to Iran's UN delegation, however, IRNA that no new round of negotiations is currently scheduled and that Tehran is awaiting a U.S. response through Qatari mediators. Iran files ICAO complaint over U.S. flight restrictions: Iran a formal complaint with the International Civil Aviation Organization over U.S. flight restrictions and is pursuing the restoration of routes suspended by several countries. Iran's CAO chief told state media Iran is working through diplomatic and legal channels to restore flights, including to Baghdad and Najaf, with Najaf expected to resume services "in the coming days." The U.S. sanctioned 27 Iranian airlines on September 8 and threatened secondary sanctions against airports and companies providing Iranian aircraft with fuel, landing services or ticket sales. Oman and the UAE have since suspended Iranian flights, while four Iraqi airports have halted them. Iraq's ambassador to Iran Monday that Najaf airport would resume Iranian flights within 24 hours, adding that Iraq had not ordered flights suspended but foreign ground-service companies had stopped servicing Iranian aircraft. Eight U.S. Marines injured in previously undisclosed Iranian missile attack in Strait of Hormuz: Eight U.S. Marines were in an Iranian anti-ship cruise missile attack on a vessel they were operating aboard in the Strait of Hormuz on September 14, NBC reported. The Marines suffered smoke inhalation and possible traumatic brain injuries, including concussion symptoms such as headaches, but returned to duty soon afterward. Officials declined to identify the type of vessel involved but said it was not a U.S. Navy ship. The Pentagon's Defense Casualty Analysis System added the eight Marines to its casualty count nearly ten days after the attack. The database now records 861 U.S. service members injured in the war with Iran. Iran it struck 19 ships in the Strait of Hormuz over the past two nights. Iranian officials said any ship crossing without authorization will face an armed response. Five arrested near UK airbase used for U.S. strikes on Iran: Five men were arrested on suspicion of preparing a "terrorist" act near RAF Fairford, a military airbase in western England used by U.S. forces to launch attacks on Iran. Armed police made the arrests early Sunday after receiving reports of three suspicious vehicles apparently heading toward the base. President Donald Trump claimed the suspects intended to do "big damage" and said British and U.S. authorities were investigating. Police have not identified a suspected motive or said who they believe was involved, and no charges have been filed. Asked whether Iran could be involved, UK Defense Secretary Wes Streeting it would be "very unwise" to speculate. The Iranian Embassy in the UK "categorically rejects and strongly condemns" speculation linking Iran to the incident. IRGC claims seizure of U.S. underwater vehicle in Hormuz: The IRGC Navy it seized a second unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV) in the Strait of Hormuz "through a coordinated and complex operation involving intelligence superiority and electronic warfare." Iran identified it as a U.S. Navy's MK18 Mod 2 Kingfish, which is primarily designed for mine clearance. The U.S. military rejected Tehran's claim. Middle East oil exports rebound as Saudi shipments surge: Crude exports from major Middle Eastern producers are on track to reach 12.8 million barrels per day (bpd) in September, their highest level since the U.S.-Israel war with Iran began, according to . The rebound was driven by increased Saudi and UAE shipments and a recovery in flows through the Strait of Hormuz, though exports remain well below February's 18.8 million bpd. Saudi exports are expected to reach about 5.4 million bpd this month, up from 2.45 million in August, as the kingdom diverted shipments from the Red Sea port of Yanbu following attacks on its East-West pipeline. Despite these rosy export projections, . U.S. Treasury yields hit new post-financial crisis highs on both the as mortgage rates climbed above 7%. Pezeshkian brings tons of pharmaceutical supplies from India as Iran faces medicine shortages: President Masoud Pezeshkian his visit to India for the BRICS summit this month to transport several tons of pharmaceutical ingredients back to Iran on his private plane, The Financial Times reported. "In the past, shortages were mainly limited to biological medicines or medications for difficult-to-treat diseases," a pharmacist in Tehran told the FT. "Now, even basic painkillers and very common psychiatric medications are unavailable." Yemen Seven killed, 40 injured in Saudi strike on Taiz: Seven people were killed and 40 others, including children, in a at the Mawiya junction in Yemen's Taiz province on Sunday. The Ansarallah Health Ministry said Saudi airstrikes hit commercial shops at the market. Yemen's Saudi-backed government claimed its own forces targeted an Ansarallah military camp and vehicles at Mawiya. 164 people were killed and 645 injured in Yemen between September 19 and 26, according to the World Health Organization. Since August 6, WHO has documented 838 deaths among 4,481 casualties. Fighting has also displaced more than 180,000 people. EU 's Kallas calls for more ships for Red Sea mission as Ansarallah expand control: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called on member states to provide more ships to the bloc's Aspides naval mission to protect Red Sea shipping, saying she has pushed for reinforcements but received no firm commitments. The EU launched Aspides in February 2024 to protect commercial vessels from attacks in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and surrounding waters. Recent territorial advances have left Ansarallah positioned around 20 kilometers from the African coast and with effective control over the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, four Palestinians were killed and 19 injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 is now 74,022 killed, with 175,980 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,421 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,983, while 834 bodies have been recovered. Israeli strike kills woman, wounds several others in Gaza City: An Israeli airstrike a home that was sheltering displaced Palestinians in northern Gaza City, according to WAFA, killing a Palestinian woman and wounding several others. Israeli settlers attack Palestinian olive harvest amid occupied West Bank closure: Israeli authorities imposed a week-long closure across the occupied West Bank on Sunday, tightening restrictions at checkpoints and military barriers, citing Jewish holidays. Ramallah and Al-Bireh: Settlers olives from Palestinian land in Sinjil, Turmus Ayya and Umm Safa, while others set fire to a Palestinian-owned vehicle in Deir Abu Mashal. The attacks come as the olive harvest begins, a period during which Palestinian farmers frequently face attacks on their trees, crops, and access to agricultural land. Jenin: Settlers entered agricultural land in Khirbet Masoud with tractors and stole harvested olives, according to WAFA. Nablus: Israeli settlers a 75-year-old Palestinian man while he was on his land in Sebastia, northwest of Nablus, beating him and pouring boiling water on his body, WAFA reported. Hebron: Israeli forces the town of Al-Samu and the Bir Haram Al-Rama area of Hebron alongside settlers. In Masafer Yatta, settlers cut and stole electricity cables. Katz, Ben-Gvir lead over 1,270 Israelis into Al-Aqsa Mosque compound: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir at least 1,271 Israelis into the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound on Monday, on the third day of the Jewish holiday of Sukkot. Groups performed religious rituals under heavy Israeli police protection. Israeli settlers attack home of Palestinian-American in the occupied West Bank: Israeli settlers attacked the home of 78-year-old Palestinian-American Mustafa Zaater and his wife on Sunday in Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, setting fire to three of his vehicles, smashing doors and windows, and attempting to enter the house. Zaater told Drop Site contributor Mutasem Sqf ElHait that dozens of settlers, some carrying weapons, approached from the northern and southern sides of the area at around 1:30 a.m. "They want to drive us out of here," Zaater said. "This is our land and our property. We're not going to give it to them and leave." Residents eventually pushed the settlers back, Abu Falah village council member Omar Hamayel, adding that Israeli forces fired tear gas at them after the settlers had withdrawn.Watch Sqf ElHait 's dispatch . Ben-Gvir threatens Palestinian prisoner with execution: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir published Sunday showing him inside the prison cell of Palestinian prisoner Hassan Salama, telling him: "I want to kill you. ... I want you executed." Salama, 55, has been imprisoned since 1996 and is serving 48 life sentences over his alleged role in a series of Hamas-orchestrated attacks. He has spent a total of more than 14 years in solitary confinement. The Palestinian Prisoners' Society condemned Ben-Gvir's threat, saying it reflected a broader Israeli policy rather than an isolated act and warning that such public threats could precede attempts to kill Palestinian prisoner leaders. Netanyahu secretly visited UAE, asked president to deny report he warned him before October 7 attack: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to the UAE on Sunday for a meeting with President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, two people briefed on the trip told the Associated Press. The meeting focused on a Haaretz report that Sheikh Mohamed had warned Netanyahu of a looming Hamas attack shortly before October 7, 2023. Netanyahu asked the Emirati president to publicly deny the report, a source with firsthand knowledge of the meeting told the AP. Netanyahu's office has denied receiving such a warning. Israel revokes status of Dutch diplomats over settlement goods ban: Israel revoked the status of diplomats representing the Netherlands in Ramallah, giving them seven days to return their Israeli-issued diplomatic documents, in response to Dutch measures targeting Israeli settlements. Lebanon Israeli airstrike hits southern Lebanon as ceasefire violations continue: Israeli warplanes an airstrike on Monday between the towns of Mayfadoun and Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah in southern Lebanon's Nabatieh governorate, while Israeli artillery targeted the outskirts of Zibqin and valleys near Yater, according to Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA). Hezbollah chief calls for halt to direct Israel talks, says disarmament must follow Israeli withdrawal: Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem called Sunday for Lebanon to freeze direct negotiations with Israel and return to "indirect" talks, while saying Hezbollah is prepared to discuss the state's monopoly on weapons only after Israel withdraws from Lebanese territory. Qassem called the U.S.-sponsored Framework Agreement a "shameful concession of all the cards" Lebanon could use to secure its rights and accused the government of "helping the Israeli-American project instead of confronting it." He said the president has the right to negotiate, but not to "give up Lebanon's right to defend its land." Qassem said Hezbollah is "ready for dialogue and discussion" over its weapons but insisted the "liberation of the south" must come first. Qassem also pledged Hezbollah would contribute to shelter and reconstruction efforts in southern Lebanon and said it would soon announce its participation in a housing project. U.S. News Troy Jackson defies consultants, denounces Gaza genocide: Troy Jackson , the Democratic candidate running against Sen. Susan Collins , has been instructed by his campaign consultants to moderate his language around Israel's genocide in Gaza and to call for an end merely to "offensive weapons," according to new reporting from Drop Site, which builds on an investigation by New York magazine. Yet at a candidate event on Saturday, he was directly pressed on the question and did not back off his previous stance, saying he believes Israel is committing a genocide in Gaza and that he won't send further aid to the state of Israel. . Susan Collins bribery scandal mushrooming: is out with a scathing editorial blasting Collins for her flailing response to ProPublica's bribery investigation: "It is extremely disappointing to watch Collins and members of her staff move to immediately discredit a thorough and fair piece of investigative journalism on political and personal grounds." The headline is harsh: "It's Maine's turn to be concerned about Susan Collins." New poll has Abdul El-Sayed leading Mike Rogers 48-44%, Trump badly underwater: The survey, by the Senate Democratic super PAC, finds Democrat Abdul El-Sayed at 48% and Republican Mike Rogers at 44% among 800 likely Michigan voters in the U.S. Senate race--outside the margin of error. The survey also finds Trump's job approval in Michigan at 37%, with 61% disapproving. Asked which concern better describes them, 51% said they were more concerned that Rogers "won't stand up to Trump," compared with 38% who said El-Sayed is "too risky for the economy." Iowa Senate candidate Ashley Hinson reaches new levels of Iran war incoherence: At a press conference in Iowa, Rep. Ashley Hinson said she texted House Speaker Mike Johnson urging him to call the House back into session to push for a "resolution to end the war" but stressed that she did not want to vote on another war powers resolution to end the war, which she has already voted against four times. "We don't need another resolution on the House floor," "We need a resolution to end the war as quickly as possible and the president can do that and I trust also our US military, the best fighting force in the world, to make sure we put every option on the table to get that done, but it needs to come to an immediate and successful end." Idaho Republican senator mum on candidate debates: The League of Conservation Voters between now and election day, but incumbent Republican Jim Risch has yet to agree to join. In a sign of the expanding Senate map, Risch faces a credible challenge from independent antiwar candidate Todd Achilles , whose recent viral ad mimics a 1980s corporate instructional video, . Angie Nixon calls for data center moratorium unless the project is built on Trump 's property: The Florida Democratic Senate candidate "I think there needs to be a moratorium until more research is done. Or if people want to build a data center, they should put it on Mar-a-Lago." Angie Nixon remains badly outspent, . New poll finds Darline Graham, Lindsey 's sister, at risk of losing South Carolina Senate seat: Pediatrician Annie Andrews is within a , giving Democrats flashbacks to the 2020 challenge to Graham by Jaime Harrison , who blew threw a staggering $130 million to lose by 10 points. Key differences in 2026: the environment is far worse for Republicans, Darline Graham is less popular than her brother, and Harrison served as South Carolina Democratic Party chair, making it impossible to distance himself from the party. Andrews is running as a more independent figure. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Myanmar military airstrike kills at least 33 people in Rakhine state: At least 33 people were and 36 injured in a military airstrike near a market in Kyauktaw, a town in western Myanmar's Rakhine state controlled by the Arakan Army, according to the rebel group and a local aid worker. Local aid worker Wai Hun Aung said the strike hit an area "quite far from the fighting" and unrelated to active combat. The Arakan Army said the attack was among the deadliest airstrikes in Rakhine since a December 2025 strike on a hospital that killed at least 30 people. Pro-government forces capture strategic Tigray town as Ethiopia fighting escalates: Ethiopia's military and allied militias announced that they have Alamata, a key supply hub about 120 km south of Tigray's capital Mekelle, Reuters . The reported capture would reverse some of the gains made by Tigrayan forces after they launched a new offensive last week and comes amid the most serious fighting since the 2022 Pretoria peace agreement ended Ethiopia's devastating civil war. Ethiopia's military has accused Eritrea, Sudan's armed forces and Egypt of backing opposition forces. Internet and phone service in Tigray has also remained disrupted for several days. In separate fighting in the country this week Ethiopia's military said it inflicted heavy losses on Tigrayan forces during fighting in northern Amhara and Afar. Serbia 's president Vučic resigns, positioning himself to return as prime minister: President Aleksandar Vučic Sunday, seven months before his final term expired, allowing him to become prime minister if his Serbian Progressive Party forms a government after the October 25 snap parliamentary election. Parliamentary Speaker Ana Brnabić will serve as interim president, with a presidential vote to follow by December. The parliamentary election will pit Vučić's ruling bloc against Students Win, an anti-corruption movement, and the pro-Western European Serbia alliance. South Korea summons Ukrainian envoy over disclosure of North Korean prisoner transfer : South Korea summoned Ukraine's acting ambassador and demanded an explanation and apology after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy publicly revealed that two captured North Korean soldiers had been transferred from Ukraine to South Korea. Seoul said the disclosure violated a confidentiality agreement between the two governments and accused Ukraine's presidential office of falsely denying that such an agreement existed. Zelenskyy announced at the UN General Assembly that the two North Korean soldiers had been captured while fighting for Russia in Ukraine and were later transferred to South Korea. France 's far-right National Rally expands Senate presence ahead of 2027 presidential election: Marine Le Pen's National Rally and its allies from Sunday's indirect elections with a record 14 seats in France's 348-member Senate, clearing the threshold to form an official parliamentary group for the first time. The result gives the far right additional resources and visibility as Le Pen prepares another presidential bid next year, when Emmanuel Macron leaves office. "The results have exceeded our expectations," Le Pen said, calling the outcome a "historic victory." National Rally first entered the Senate in 2014 with two seats. Ukrainian strikes force fourth Russian refinery shutdown in under a week: Ukrainian drones hit Russian refinery ablaze over the weekend, Reuters reported, as Kyiv's campaign disrupts Russian fuel exports. Before the strikes, Russia exported roughly 900,000 to 1 million barrels of diesel a day--about 10% of global supply. Kpler data now puts its net diesel exports near 100,000 barrels a day. Ukraine's General Staff said its forces also struck a missile-components plant in Azov operated by Russia's Tactical Missiles Corporation. Russia launched 173 drones overnight into Saturday and another 170 overnight into Sunday, with strikes recorded at 18 locations, according to Ukraine's air force. Attacks killed at least two people in Kyiv and the Odessa region overnight into Sunday, while Kyiv endured near-continuous attacks for a second consecutive day. RSF commander defects to Sudanese army with 50 fighters: A Rapid Support Forces commander, Al-Tayeb al-Wahidu, and 50 fighters defected to the Sudanese military in Omdurman, Drop Site's Godfrey Olukya . Sudanese army Major Ali Gubba said Saturday that the group arrived Friday in five trucks and was received by senior military and intelligence officials. Speaking to reporters, Wahidu attributed his departure to pervasive abuses within the RSF and urged other fighters to lay down their weapons and join the Sudanese armed forces. Gubba said many of the defectors belonged to the Mahamid clan, led by Musa Hilal, a former militia commander who split from the RSF and moved from North Darfur to government-held territory in February. Final U.S. troops withdraw from Iraq amid Kurdish leaders warnings: The last U.S. troops are to leave Iraq by September 30, with Kurdistan Regional Government Prime Minister Masrour Barzani warning that the departure leaves the region exposed to Iranian retaliation. "The threat is real--we are vulnerable, we are being attacked," Barzani told the Financial Times, calling the prospect of being left without air defenses "shameful." At least 1,000 Iranian drones and missiles have targeted Iraqi Kurdistan since the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran began in February, according to the regional government, primarily targeting U.S. military sites and Iranian Kurdish opposition camps. The regional government says it has no air defenses of its own and that Baghdad controls their purchase. body:
You’re invited to tonight’s Take Back The House virtual phone bank with Team Tran and special guests!

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/derektranforcongress/2026-sep-28-phone-bank-blast-6432894?e=fa48019594)
---
| | | | |
---
| | Dear Supporter,
You’re invited to tonight’s _**Take Back The House**_ virtual phone bank with Team Tran and special guests!
**WHEN:** Monday, September 28 5:30 - 7:30 p.m. PST**WHERE:** Virtual**RSVP:**[**HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/Ztdn9AR6_f6?e=fa48019594&c2id=2d2f4814b3c86de5c7569386ec1a86b4)
To receive your virtual meeting link, phone bank training, and hear from special guests, please RSVP via the link above. I hope to see you there!
Sincerely,Congressman Derek Tran
---
| | ###
_The son of refugees who worked hard and sacrificed for the American Dream, Congressman Derek Tran joined the Army at 18 to give back to the country that has given him so much. Wanting to continue his career in public service, he ran in California's 45th district to put people ahead of politics and protect democracy, and won. Now, he's running again to ensure everyone no matter what neighborhood they come from has the opportunity to succeed without fear of their freedoms being taken away._
_California’s 45th Congressional District remains one of the most contested battleground races in the country. Last cycle, Derek Tran flipped the seat by just over 600 votes (a 0.2% margin) in the second-closest and most expensive House race ($46 million spent) in the country. A majority-minority district, the District has the third largest AAPI population (41%) of any Congressional District, is 28% Latino, and is home to the largest Vietnamese community in the country. Following Proposition 50, this district brings in over 15,000 new Hispanic voters and over 7,000 new Vietnamese voters, and has a DPI of 52.8%. It includes all or part of the cities of Garden Grove, Westminster, Fountain Valley, Cerritos, Buena Park, Placentia, Hawaiian Gardens, Cypress, Artesia, Los Alamitos, La Palma, Norwalk, Stanton, Lakewood, Santa Ana, Seal Beach, and Fullerton, as well as the unincorporated community of Midway City._
_Use of Derek Tran's military rank, job titles, and photographs in uniform does not imply endorsement by the Dept. of Defense or U.S. Army._

name: Kailee Buller
subject: Our FINAL report card
body:
This is the last End-of-Quarter deadline before Election Day.

| | | | |
---
| | | | | |
FINAL END OF QUARTER DEADLINE: **SEPTEMBER 30TH**
[ CHIP IN NOW >>](https://us.list-manage.com/ySOy9wJ_cWp?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

Peter,
It's that time again, and this time, _it's the last one._
At the end of every three months, campaigns across the country submit their fundraising totals to the Federal Election Commission (FEC). But these Quarterly Reports do a lot more than tell the FEC who donated.
_They're a campaign's report card._
They show the media, House leadership, and my opponent how healthy and competitive our campaign really is. **And Peter this is our FINAL End-of-Quarter report before Election Day.** There are no more chances after this. The final countdown has begun.
That's why we've set our most important goal yet: $25,000 before midnight on September 30.
[**HELP US HIT $25,000 BEFORE THE FINAL DEADLINE →**](https://us.list-manage.com/lYc1nllnFNr?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
A strong report tells everyone watching that Central New York is ready for change, and that this seat is ready to FLIP. A weak one tells the Democrat Machine they can coast to November.
_I grew up in Auburn in a blue-collar family. I know what it means to work hard, do everything right, and still wonder why it keeps getting harder to get ahead. I'm running to lower costs, back law enforcement, protect our family farms, and give President Trump another reliable America First vote in the House._
But none of that happens unless we finish this race strong.
[**Will you chip in $26, $50, $100, or whatever you can to help us earn an A+ on our final report card?**](https://us.list-manage.com/DGk35hARbfo?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---
| [RUSH A DONATION NOW >>](https://us.list-manage.com/MODepUAA9m8?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
---
| |
**Peter, I know your inbox is full right now. Every campaign in the country is racing toward this same deadline. But this race is one of the best opportunities in the nation to expand President Trump's House majority, and your support matters more here than almost anywhere.**
The deadline is midnight on September 30. [Let's show them exactly how strong we are.](https://us.list-manage.com/Wc4RGcXTubK?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
Thank you,
Kailee BullerRepublican Candidate for Congress, NY-22

subject: Texas is the top target. I need you to know that
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ted Cruz for Senate
body:
This one's for you personally

I tried to unwind this weekend. I really did. I told myself I wasn't going to think about the election, or the Trump administration, or any of the hundred other things that have been pissing me off lately. I was going to sit on my couch, watch some football with my kiddo like a normal human being.
And then, right as the games were getting good, the screen cut away to a slow-motion montage of Donald Trump. Swelling music. Flags. A narrator telling me how lucky I am to be living through this glorious moment in American history.
God damn it.
And no, I'm not talking about him showing up at the Tennessee game. I don't particularly care about that. That's his prerogative. Go eat a hot dog, wave at the jumbotron, whatever. I'm talking about these insane ads.
What I'm pissed off about is that, over and over again, they used your money and my money -- _our_ taxpayer dollars -- to air what are obviously illegal campaign ads on national television. Because for two years, these people have lectured us about waste, fraud, and abuse. They've taken a chainsaw to programs people actually rely on and told us it was necessary to protect the American taxpayer. Money for housing assistance, adult education, schools, national parks, cancer research for kids (that last one pisses me off the most) -- apparently we need to tighten our belts.
But Donald Trump needs a television commercial? Break out the damn checkbook.
What a slap in the face. This administration keeps telling working people that government can't afford to help them, while somehow always finding money when it serves their Supreme Leader.
They're so desperate to hold on in the midterms that they're now openly abusing their power in a way that is stupid, foolish, and so transparent that I'm honestly embarrassed for them.
Every time one of these ads came on, it filled me with more rage. And not one of them convinced a single person in this country that this administration is solving a problem that might actually improve their life. If anything, I think these ads are going to backfire simply because of the sheer arrogance required to make them in the first place.
People don't like watching their tax dollars get spent on a politician's vanity reel. And the way these people think Americans are spectacularly stupid should irritate the shit out of every single one of us. Including their own voters. Especially their own voters. Because that's how they treat them.
Here's the thing: these ads could not be more ineffective if they tried.
One of them tells you Donald Trump is removing all the warmongers from Washington, D.C.
Let that sink in for a second.
This is the man waging an illegal war in Iran right now. At least 22 American service members are dead. 22 families got that knock on the door. 22 empty chairs at the dinner table this fall. And God knows how many more there will be once we finally get an honest number. Meanwhile, he's manipulating the market and profiteering off of it, while the rest of us eat the cost of the global economic and energy crisis he created.
And he has the nerve to use your money to buy airtime during a football game, to call himself the guy who ended the warmongering.
It's absolutely sickening.

* * *
And then there's the line they keep hammering in these ads: America will never be taken over by communism. America will never become a communist country.
There is no greater communist in American history who has achieved power than Donald Trump. And these ads prove that point. They are straight out of the Chinese Communist playbook. They look like they could be airing in North Korea right now. Glossy, government-funded tributes to the Dear Leader, jammed between downs. And this is the guy warning YOU about communism?
He's hosting giant dinners with the president of China and the big tech billionaires bankrolling Republican campaigns. He's offering to sell weapons to the Chinese at the very moment the Chinese are helping prop up Iran in a war nobody wanted in the first place.
And while he's doing all that, his family is cashing in on their positions in government. He's taking public stakes in private companies.
That's socialism, guys.
At least, it's the kind of socialism I've been told my whole life to be terrified of. Except apparently it's totally fine when you use the full power of the federal government to make one rich family even richer. What you can't do, God forbid, is use that same power to make sure you don't go bankrupt when you get sick. Or to make sure you get a fair day's wage for an honest day's work. Or to build a social safety net that takes care of the least among us.
Oh no. Not that. That's the scary kind.
But socialism for the wealthy? Socialism for big tech billionaires? Socialism for the Trump family business? Step right up.
They don't actually seem to have a problem with government spending. They have a problem with who it gets spent on and who it serves.
So here's where I land, and you know how I end these things.
Take that rage. Take whatever you're feeling right now, the anger, the disgust, the exhaustion, and turn it into something meaningful. We have one month left until this election. They're on the run. They're scared shitless. You can smell the desperation on them in every move they make, including this one.
They've got your tax dollars to spend on propaganda. We don't. What we have is each other.
So here's how we split the work. You make the calls, chip in to a campaign, find a race and plug in. And I'll keep doing what I do: calling this out every single week, loudly and without apology, so you never feel like you're the only one who sees it. If Endless Urgency is part of how you stay sane and fired up, become a paid subscriber today. That's what keeps this independent, and it's what keeps us in this fight long after the next 30 days.
I'm sure they love the idea that they triggered another lib this weekend. Let them enjoy it. Because the days of triggering the libs are over.
The American people are pissed. And they're coming for them at the ballot box.
With urgency,
--Mike

We're the closest race in the country. Nate Silver's model showed Michigan's 4th as the tightest margin of any House, Senate, or Governor's race in America — 0.1%!! 3. The national GOP is dumping millions into this race. They noticed our momentum too. Trump's super PAC is spending more here than in almost any other House race in the country, and the national GOP has launched millions of dollars in misleading attack ads against Sean. 4. We have our final end-of-quarter FEC deadline on September 30. name: Scott Kelly
subject: Humbly requesting you
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
#

Hello,
It’s Scott Kelly — Mark Kelly’s twin brother (also an astronaut!).
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260928-2-b&refcode2=11875.3935704.ma2w3L&t=1&akid=11875%2E3935704%2Ema2w3L)_(I'm the one on the left.)_
I know Mark and Gabby pretty well, better than most. To know them is to know one thing: **_Don’t ever — not even for one moment — underestimate them._**
On January 8, 2011, I was commanding the International Space Station (ISS) when Gabby was shot at a constituent event. It rocked our family forever.
Throughout the next few weeks, I called Mark every day on the phone as he updated me on Gabby’s condition. I traveled to see them immediately after landing.
I am in awe of Gabby. It’s now been fifteen years since that terrible day, but Gabby hasn’t stopped fighting — not only for herself, but for our families across the country.
But the truth is, not everybody likes that. That’s exactly why the NRA is working so hard to attack Gabby and the incredible work she’s accomplished at GIFFORDS.
It’s never easy watching your family get attacked, but I’m so grateful to know you have their back. Together, you have helped them stand up to the gun lobby and pass more than 820 gun safety laws. That’s no small feat.
**But as the attacks ramp up ahead of the midterm elections, Gabby can’t win this fight alone. So I have a humble request:**
[**Will you please chip in $5 to stand with Gabby? GIFFORDS PAC is working to reach undecided voters and take on the gun lobby’s influence in our politics, but she needs your help before their FEC deadline in 72 hours >>**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260928-2-b&amount=5&t=2&akid=11875%2E3935704%2Ema2w3L)

| | **[Donate $50](https://go.giffords.org/go/17010?c0=giff-em-q32026.UqOZLu&refcode=em260928-2-b&t=23&akid=11875%2E3935704%2Ema2w3L)**

| | **[Donate $250](https://go.giffords.org/go/17012?c0=giff-em-q32026.0vxkI7&refcode=em260928-2-b&t=25&akid=11875%2E3935704%2Ema2w3L)**

---
****
I don’t reach out often, so when I do, I hope you know it’s important. Thank you in advance for supporting Gabby in this fight.
Thank you,
Scott Kelly

**Please, take a second to read this...**
GIFFORDS has been on the front lines to save lives from gun violence for more than a decade, but we can’t do it alone.
If everyone reading this donated just $17, we'd have the resources to pass commonsense gun safety legislation across the country. But not everyone gives — making it even more important for people who care and understand the stakes of our struggle to pitch in what they can.
**If $17 seems worth it to you to change our gun laws in order to make our communities safer from gun violence, we're asking you to stand with Gabby Giffords and donate to GIFFORDS PAC today.**

Every state levies taxes and runs welfare. What California has done this decade is quietly dissolve the boundary between the two and citizenship itself -- and never put the question to the taxpayers. The result is a shadow welfare state: the nation's largest safety net, more than $180 billion a year, extended past its legal limits and financed by the highest tax rates in America.
Start with what the system actually covers. Reporters who visited four public-services offices in Southern California found officials remarkably candid. In Glendale, a welfare officer described CAPI -- the Cash Assistance Program for Immigrants, a state-funded substitute for SSI -- this way: "If [you are] a citizen, you cannot get CAPI... I don't care about legal or not. Not being [a] citizen [is the key]." Consider that: a benefit for the destitute and disabled that citizens cannot have. In Los Angeles, another officer explained the CalWORKs arithmetic -- an illegal-immigrant mother with U.S.-born children gets "money for the child, and not for her." The benefits stack: Medi-Cal, CalWORKs, Section 8, college grants, tax credits, subsidized car insurance, free phones. By my arithmetic, one family of five -- two illegal-alien parents, two U.S.-born children, an illegal-alien grandparent -- can draw public services worth more than $100,000 a year.

When I served as Governor of Wisconsin, I knew that safer communities depended on strong prosecutors doing the hard work every single day.
| | | | [](https://link.action.erictoney.)

| When I served as Governor of Wisconsin, we relied on strong prosecutors doing the hard work every single day to keep our streets safe.
Eric Toney became Fond du Lac County District Attorney in 2013, during my first term as governor.
While our administration was working for a stronger, more prosperous Wisconsin, Eric was in the courtroom handling serious cases, including homicides, sexual assaults, domestic violence, violent crime, gun crime, and financial crimes.

_**Eric understands that public safety is about solving problems before they become even bigger ones.**_
[Please join me in supporting Eric by making a $100 donation today. Wisconsin has backslid under Democrat control, and it's time we elect a competent leader to deliver justice to victims and fix the crime labs, once and for all.](https://link.action.erictoney.)
He helped bring a Drug Court to Fond du Lac County and was part of the group that developed the Fond du Lac County Opioid Coalition as communities across Wisconsin confronted the opioid crisis.
His leadership extended beyond his own county. Eric became a leader in the Wisconsin District Attorneys Association, working with prosecutors from across the state on the challenges facing Wisconsin’s criminal justice system.

Those are the kinds of experiences that matter: _doing the work, knowing the system, supporting victims, and understanding what prosecutors and law enforcement need to keep Wisconsin communities safe._
Wisconsin has always been strongest when serious people are willing to step forward, take responsibility, and get results. Eric Toney has spent his career doing exactly that.

Please join me in supporting him and _[donate to his campaign today.](https://link.action.erictoney.)_
Sincerely,
---
45th Governor of Wisconsin Scott Walker

_**-- Cliff**_
* * *
Here's last week in one sentence: Republicans spent it running--from reporters, from a vote, and from their own voters' health care. Mike Johnson sent the House home for seven weeks rather than let members vote on Thomas Massie's articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth. The White House started throwing reporters out of the building. And JD Vance kicked 750,000 people off Obamacare to fight "fraud," holding up a case that, as Jonathan Larsen found, started on Trump's watch.
Meanwhile, the map kept moving our way. A Democrat is leading in Kansas. Every indicator in Matt Robison's Midterm HQ dashboard moved blue, and the GOP is pouring $110 million into emergency defense. That is not a party playing offense. Five weeks out, the only way we blow this is by getting comfortable, which is exactly why Joe Walsh told us to work like we're down. Here's everything you missed.
## Monday, September 21
* **[Is Trump Headed for Dunkirk or Waterloo?](https://substack.com/redirect/a94c099b-0553-4fdb-b7ee-5eb2f36eaf97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** --Cliff maps a Senate battlefield so wide that even a cautious Democratic senator is now saying nine seats. The headline: a Democrat, Adam Hamilton, leads Roger Marshall in Kansas, a state that hasn't elected a Democratic senator since 1932.

## Tuesday, September 22
* **[Pete Hegseth Is Toast](https://substack.com/redirect/6bcef105-eb1b-4409-abca-f1d787ecb138?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** --David Shuster on Rep. Thomas Massie's eight articles of impeachment against the defense secretary, and why Speaker Johnson recessed the House for seven weeks rather than hold the vote.

## Wednesday, September 23
* **[The Blue Letter: Trump Crashes Below 30% Approval](https://substack.com/redirect/582be0ec-b2e0-43bb-956f-c8f7e8a2cd1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** --Cliff's paid-member letter on a president under fire from his own party and lashing out at the press as the midterms slip away.
* **[Banning Reporters Doesn't Do What Trump Thinks It Does](https://substack.com/redirect/27ae766c-0d0d-4def-bbdf-5a49feddd6db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**--The White House went after CNN, MS NOW, and Politico. David Shuster, who worked that briefing room, explains why the real reporting never happened there anyway.

## Thursday, September 24
* **[The Feds Say Their Phone-Cracking Software Was Secretly Russian](https://substack.com/redirect/68596226-ab72-45fd-8429-1bbec70c45bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** --On _Amped Up_ , Olga Lautman joins Cliff and David. Months ago she exposed Oxygen Forensics; now the Justice Department has charged its CEO with hiding the company's Russian ownership.

## Friday, September 25
* **[Prosecutors Are Probing Epstein's Lawyer and Accountant](https://substack.com/redirect/5d559d86-1a14-4c2e-aa9b-d5458818eef8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**--Kait Justice, a year into the Epstein files, tells Cliff and David what Epstein's longtime lawyer and accountant would know--and why prosecutors are now asking.
* **[Trump BANS the Press--Satirists Take It from There](https://substack.com/redirect/3f4ce219-d7db-451f-9775-71b9fec165b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**--David's weekly countdown of the top five AI political satire videos, from press-room parodies to a fictional Trump TV network.

## Saturday, September 26
* **[The GOP Just Got Sacked](https://substack.com/redirect/7effb4b8-74a7-4aa6-b709-698819150cfb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** --Matt Robison's Midterm HQ dashboard: a blue sweep across polls, ratings, and prediction markets; a $110 million tell; and two races to watch closely.
* **[Joe Walsh: Ignore the Polls and Work Like You're Down](https://substack.com/redirect/371ea914-c5c9-4dfb-94b1-d2d779555946?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**--On _Tequila Talk_ , Cliff and Joe Walsh on why Republican money can't buy back voters who've made up their minds, and the one Senate race Democrats could still find a way to lose.

Five weeks out, this is the ammunition. Subscribe and read the whole week. -- Cliff Here's last week in one sentence: Republicans spent it running--from reporters, from a vote, and from their own voters' health care. Mike Johnson sent the House home for seven weeks rather than let members vote on Thomas Massie's articles of impeachment against Pete Hegseth. The White House started throwing reporters out of the building. And JD Vance kicked 750,000 people off Obamacare to fight "fraud," holding up a case that, as Jonathan Larsen found, started on Trump's watch. Meanwhile, the map kept moving our way. | | Dear Friend,

Here's a story I'll never forget, once I learned the truth behind it.

In 1917, a small group of revolutionaries led by Vladimir Lenin seized power in Russia. They promised a better, fairer world...sound familiar?

But soon after taking control, they began rounding up and executing anyone who stood in their way. Lenin even ordered his followers to hang landowners and seize their crops--so that for miles around, "people see, and tremble..."

Marxism began with promises of a perfect world--and ended in fear, famine, and death.

You may be familiar with that dark history, but too many Americans aren't. How do I know?

Because a century later, these dangerous ideas have been repackaged and rebranded. They're taught in schools and promoted by celebrity politicians using words such as "equity," "diversity," and "social justice."

The words sound harmless, but the ideas behind them are the same. Will they end up with the same terrifying results?

That's why Hillsdale College has created the National Quiz on Marxism, Socialism, and Communism, and I'd love for you to take it.

You can complete your National Quiz on Marxism, Socialism, and Communism using this secure link:

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/marxism-quiz-tf](http://links.redconservatives.com/s/c/zdxKreVvLTr4kEPxx_sJowT_hEfKSaJoa4F5sInuWHkilb1ho1Q6pnnz0RI6Y9MARBSHsTl_lEU5ZZsiwjLmdUzMi9XFJDQ7BRkxSQFn-Ou9JX1t5TfjcDeSNsH2vZIdaHzI54FOnWxAxKBrGb4kD9CG0A7gPb62Ur8mVHdjrJi7yGBBPcxkR-DUVtEgTvL5WdMfkuaSsXh_uk71yhgH7yuXXuFiXfBbBmxk4FDYYxhzWnXyVZ787tVYJ8rZ5KGUh6EzT-lrWdqqP2M59Qxsw0eC_OZwcjmbv_8notOKLNRcl7gRIBpdFBvO5NLytk_jEMpiSZVZmufh-jFJvGa32XyT-ivSJvqURcU1s1Q6NYeKqb_kmAp2Zit4kMC1xm9GhwIhqET4tuFCgS1yWd-d5Kppn-acjHbKptjVM7rONBndKtF0VMa-hgi11-G_jrSemrLOmFxnReM_XOXlwD2mgyIACyLH-iHVbxh_P36JGE3y0XWGY00WkqiTTZvYTJASpE7bauG4AwAx8gpZ4EIDvl7S_VyNxGcW9WPG8UWX7hIfvceEYgDc6Wg5C62uUu9Of23tRH40ecjDkB0oa8QUgHGKFMLjJAo6YyjFlk5z9TJJfSI6d5twzBlHKo2aLxub4-TSRkm9YwFi4Y4BeG5Ar4K-U7lgXwcBta93E8aYZ-YN2xCc7v8AqWYzdlSbTsRoDmuf/z7Ii3UKCiGz-gxMfjkH6WNNpg3eEYG-p/25)

Most young Americans have never learned this history. I know I didn't in high school. But you can help change that with your financial support today.

clean_body: Marxism began with promises of a perfect world—and ended in fear, famine, and death. | | Please see a special message from our sponsor. If you would like to unsubscribe, visit this | | | Dear Friend, Here's a story I'll never forget, once I learned the truth behind it. In 1917, a small group of revolutionaries led by Vladimir Lenin seized power in Russia. They promised a better, fairer world...sound familiar? But soon after taking control, they began rounding up and executing anyone who stood in their way. Lenin even ordered his followers to hang landowners and seize their crops--so that for miles around, "people see, and tremble..." Marxism began with promises of a perfect world--and ended in fear, famine, and death. You may be familiar with that dark history, but too many Americans aren't. How do I know? Because a century later, these dangerous ideas have been repackaged and rebranded. They're taught in schools and promoted by celebrity politicians using words such as "equity," "diversity," and "social justice." The words sound harmless, but the ideas behind them are the same. Will they end up with the same terrifying results? That's why Hillsdale College has created the National Quiz on Marxism, Socialism, and Communism, and I'd love for you to take it. You can complete your National Quiz on Marxism, Socialism, and Communism using this secure link: This short quiz will test your knowledge of the history and real-world consequences of dangerous ideologies like Marxism and socialism. And when you finish, we'll email you the answers, and you can watch our free online documentary-style course, "Marxism, Socialism, and Communism," which tells the whole story--from Lenin's Red Terror to today's Cultural Marxism. Most young Americans have never learned this history. I know I didn't in high school. But you can help change that with your financial support today. young people who are misled by the same false ideas that once brought such misery to Russia and the world. Because of you, more Americans will learn that the principles of liberty in the Declaration of Independence--not Marxism--are the true path to ordered freedom and human flourishing. Good luck on the quiz. Warm regards, Bill Gray, '01 Vice President Institutional Advancement Hillsdale College P.S. Lenin's revolution began with promises of equality but ended with terror. Everyone Says ‘Your Move.’ Somebody at This Table Is Bluffing.
Tehran says it’s ready for a ‘doomsday war.’ Trump says talks are coming this week. Oil sided with Tehran before breakfast — and a runaway AI agent just joined the game.
Threat level 4/5 — Elevated
